children.text: Code Geass is officially returning with a new anime, Code Geass: Star Chaser Aspal. After being announced in December 2025 as part of the franchise’s 20th-anniversary plans, the project received its first teaser trailer and a 2027 release window in September 2026.

The footage gives fans their first real look at what appears to be a very different corner of the Code Geass world. Instead of immediately returning to the familiar political imagery of Britannia, the teaser uses an older-looking battlefield, arrows, armored figures and enormous humanoid machines. Sunrise has not yet explained the setting, timeline or characters.
When Does Code Geass: Star Chaser Aspal Release?

Code Geass: Star Chaser Aspal is scheduled for 2027. The official teaser site lists the project for 2027, but no exact premiere date, month or season has been announced. Any more specific date should therefore be treated as speculation until Sunrise or the official Code Geass channels confirm it.

The 2027 window is the biggest new piece of information since the anime was first announced at the Code Geass Project “To 20th” event on December 7, 2025. That event confirmed the title and core staff but did not provide a release window.
What Does the First Teaser Show?

The September 2026 teaser is deliberately cryptic. It shows a harsh battlefield filled with arrows and combat, along with large humanoid machines. The imagery has a noticeably different atmosphere from the modern military and imperial settings most viewers associate with Lelouch of the Rebellion.

The teaser also hints at the supernatural side of the franchise, but it does not explain who possesses Geass, what form that power takes here, or how the new story connects to previous entries. Those unanswered questions are likely intentional.

One important term in the announced staff credits is Agarmata. Yoshi. is specifically credited with Agarmata design. The teaser includes giant mechanical-looking figures, but official material has not yet explained what Agarmata are or how they differ from the franchise’s familiar Knightmare Frames. Calling every machine in the teaser a Knightmare Frame would go beyond what has been confirmed.
Is Star Chaser Aspal a Sequel to Lelouch of the Rebellion?

Sunrise has not confirmed Star Chaser Aspal as a direct sequel to Lelouch of the Rebellion, Lelouch of the Re;surrection or Rozé of the Recapture. It is a completely new Code Geass animation project, but its exact continuity has not been explained.

That distinction matters because Code Geass already has multiple continuity layers. The original Lelouch of the Rebellion and R2 television series form one familiar path, while the compilation-film continuity makes changes that lead into Lelouch of the Re;surrection. Akito the Exiled and Rozé of the Recapture expand the franchise through different characters and locations.

For now, viewers should avoid assuming that Star Chaser Aspal takes place before, after or parallel to any specific entry. The unusual visual setting has encouraged theories, but official material has not supplied enough evidence to place it confidently on the timeline.
Will Lelouch Be in Star Chaser Aspal?
Lelouch has not been announced as part of the cast or story. In fact, the cast itself has not been revealed yet. The same applies to C.C., Suzaku, Kallen and other established characters.

The Code Geass name understandably makes Lelouch the first character many fans ask about, but Star Chaser Aspal should not be treated as a Lelouch project unless Sunrise says so. Rozé of the Recapture already showed that the franchise can build a new central cast under the wider Code Geass banner.
Who Is Making the New Code Geass Anime?

Sunrise is credited with the original work, planning and animation production. Kazuya Nomura is directing, with Mado Nozaki handling series composition. Rolua is responsible for character design, while Yoshi. is credited with Agarmata design.

Nomura has directed projects including Joker Game and Run with the Wind, while Nozaki is known for works including KADO: The Right Answer and Babylon. The announced staff and unfamiliar visual language point toward a new story rather than a simple anniversary remake.
Why Star Chaser Aspal Matters for Code Geass

Code Geass reached its 20th anniversary in 2026, but the franchise has never depended entirely on repeating Lelouch’s original rebellion. Akito the Exiled shifted the conflict to Europe, Lelouch of the Re;surrection continued the film continuity, and Rozé of the Recapture introduced another set of protagonists and political circumstances.

Star Chaser Aspal appears positioned as the next test of how far the franchise can stretch its identity. The teaser’s battlefield aesthetic raises questions about era, geography and technology. If the setting is radically different, the series could explore what makes a story feel like Code Geass even when its countries, machines and protagonists change.
How Does It Connect to Rozé of the Recapture?

No story connection has been confirmed. The timing is notable because the new teaser arrived around the conclusion of the television broadcast of Code Geass: Rozé of the Recapture in Japan, moving attention from the most recent series toward the franchise’s next project.
Until Sunrise publishes a synopsis, character names or timeline details, fans should treat Rozé and Aspal as separate projects rather than assuming one directly continues the other.
What Is Still Unknown?

Despite the teaser, Sunrise is keeping most of the story under wraps. The exact 2027 premiere date is unknown. No cast has been announced. There is no confirmed episode count, international streaming platform or detailed synopsis.

The identities of the characters shown in the visual and trailer also remain unconfirmed, as does the nature of the Agarmata. Most importantly for longtime fans, the project’s position within Code Geass continuity has not been explained.

A full trailer, cast reveal or official synopsis should tell us much more about whether Star Chaser Aspal is set in an unfamiliar historical period, an alternate world, or another part of the established Code Geass timeline.
The Short Answer

Code Geass: Star Chaser Aspal is a new Sunrise anime scheduled for 2027. Its first teaser trailer is now available, and Kazuya Nomura is directing with Mado Nozaki on series composition, Rolua on character design and Yoshi. on Agarmata design.

An exact release date, cast, episode count, streaming service and connection to Lelouch’s story have not been confirmed. The teaser gives the project a strikingly different battlefield aesthetic, but theories about its timeline and returning characters remain speculation.

children.text: Aviso de spoilers: este artículo explica la pelea de Tanjiro y Akaza en Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba - Castillo Infinito. Evita detalles posteriores del final del manga que todavía no se han adaptado al anime.

El Mundo Transparente es un estado avanzado de percepción que permite a un espadachín observar el cuerpo de un rival con un nivel de detalle extraordinario. En vez de limitarse a seguir los movimientos externos, el usuario puede percibir señales como contracciones musculares, flujo sanguíneo, respiración y cambios físicos que ocurren justo antes de un ataque.

Castillo Infinito convierte esta habilidad en uno de los avances más importantes de Tanjiro Kamado. Sin embargo, hay una confusión frecuente: el Mundo Transparente no es una nueva Respiración, tampoco es una evolución directa de la Marca del Cazador y no es exactamente lo mismo que el Estado Desinteresado.
¿Qué es el Mundo Transparente en Demon Slayer?

En términos simples, el Mundo Transparente mejora radicalmente la forma en que el usuario procesa el cuerpo y los movimientos de su oponente. Los músculos que se tensan, las articulaciones que cambian de posición, la respiración y la circulación dejan de ser procesos invisibles y se convierten en información útil para anticipar lo que va a ocurrir.

Por eso algunas escenas pueden dar la impresión de que el tiempo se ralentiza. El Mundo Transparente no detiene ni reduce literalmente el tiempo. Lo que cambia es la percepción del usuario: su concentración es tan precisa que puede procesar detalles que normalmente desaparecerían dentro de la velocidad de un combate.
¿Cómo desbloquea Tanjiro el Mundo Transparente?

Tanjiro alcanza este estado durante su enfrentamiento con Akaza al recordar a su padre, Tanjuro Kamado. De niño había visto a Tanjuro moverse con una eficiencia y una calma que todavía no podía comprender. En plena batalla, esas memorias finalmente adquieren sentido: no se trata simplemente de aumentar la fuerza, sino de eliminar movimientos innecesarios y llevar la percepción al límite.

Este avance encaja con la evolución de Tanjiro. Su olfato siempre le permitió detectar aperturas y cambios en un rival, pero el Mundo Transparente va mucho más allá de esa ventaja sensorial. Ahora puede leer señales físicas internas y utilizarlas para anticipar movimientos que antes parecían demasiado rápidos.
¿Por qué el Mundo Transparente es tan importante contra Akaza?

Akaza es especialmente peligroso porque su estilo de combate gira alrededor de leer al adversario y reaccionar con una velocidad extrema. Su Aguja Brújula detecta el espíritu de lucha del enemigo, así que enfrentarlo de manera convencional favorece precisamente el tipo de combate que él domina.

El Mundo Transparente resuelve una parte del problema: permite que Tanjiro lea mejor el cuerpo de Akaza y reaccione con mayor precisión. La otra parte depende del Estado Desinteresado, que reduce la presencia combativa que Akaza utiliza para localizar y anticipar a su oponente. Juntas, ambas ideas explican cómo Tanjiro consigue crear una apertura.
Mundo Transparente vs. Estado Desinteresado: ¿cuál es la diferencia?

Aunque aparecen estrechamente relacionados durante el avance de Tanjiro, cumplen funciones distintas. El Mundo Transparente se centra en la percepción del rival. El Estado Desinteresado se centra en el propio usuario: elimina o suprime el espíritu de lucha, la hostilidad y la intención que un enemigo como Akaza puede detectar.

La forma más fácil de recordarlo es esta: el Mundo Transparente ayuda a Tanjiro a leer a Akaza; el Estado Desinteresado dificulta que Akaza lea a Tanjiro. Que ambos sean importantes en el mismo combate ha hecho que a veces se describan erróneamente como una sola habilidad.
¿El Mundo Transparente forma parte de la Respiración del Sol?

No. El Mundo Transparente no es una forma especial de la Respiración del Sol ni del Hinokami Kagura. Tanjiro utiliza el Hinokami Kagura mucho antes de comprender plenamente este estado, y otros espadachines pueden acceder al Mundo Transparente sin utilizar la Respiración del Sol.

Demon Slayer tiene varias mejoras avanzadas que pueden aparecer juntas sin ser la misma habilidad. Los estilos de respiración determinan gran parte de la técnica de combate; la Marca del Cazador aumenta las capacidades físicas bajo determinadas condiciones; el Mundo Transparente mejora la percepción; y una espada Nichirin roja tiene efectos propios contra los demonios.
Para entender mejor la base de esas técnicas, puedes consultar nuestra guía de los
estilos de respiración de Demon Slayer
¿El Mundo Transparente aparece gracias a la Marca del Cazador?

Ambas habilidades aparecen en el nivel más alto del combate de Demon Slayer, pero no conviene tratar el Mundo Transparente como una simple mejora de la Marca. Sus efectos son diferentes. La Marca aumenta las capacidades físicas del espadachín, mientras que el Mundo Transparente modifica la forma en que percibe y predice el movimiento.

Esto también explica por qué desbloquear una habilidad avanzada no significa automáticamente haber conseguido todas las demás. Los cazadores excepcionales pueden reunir varias de estas capacidades, pero cada una cumple una función específica.
¿Quién puede usar el Mundo Transparente?

Tanjiro es el ejemplo central para quienes siguen el anime después de la primera película de Castillo Infinito, pero la habilidad no pertenece exclusivamente a la familia Kamado. El manga confirma que otros espadachines excepcionales pueden alcanzar el mismo estado. Entre ellos están Yoriichi Tsugikuni, Gyomei Himejima, Muichiro Tokito y Obanai Iguro, además de Tanjuro.

Esto es importante porque define el Mundo Transparente como un nivel extraordinario de percepción y dominio corporal, no como un poder hereditario reservado al protagonista. Yoriichi destaca especialmente porque su relación con esta percepción es excepcional incluso dentro de un grupo de espadachines extraordinarios.
¿El Mundo Transparente hace a Tanjiro más fuerte que un Hashira?

No de forma automática. Desbloquear esta percepción no elimina diferencias de experiencia, resistencia, velocidad, fuerza o dominio de la espada. Contra Akaza, Tanjiro obtiene una respuesta concreta a un problema concreto, pero eso no equivale a subir instantáneamente por encima de todos los Hashira.

El verdadero valor de la habilidad está en la información. Ver con mayor precisión lo que el cuerpo del rival está a punto de hacer permite reaccionar antes y atacar con más exactitud, pero el usuario todavía necesita la velocidad y la técnica necesarias para aprovechar lo que percibe.
¿Por qué vuelve tan peligroso a Tanjiro contra Akaza?

Akaza puede adaptarse a combatientes extremadamente fuertes porque su técnica le ayuda a leer el espíritu de lucha y responder a sus ataques. Tanjiro cambia las reglas del enfrentamiento: con el Mundo Transparente puede interpretar mejor los movimientos físicos de Akaza y, al mismo tiempo, con el Estado Desinteresado deja de ofrecerle la señal combativa que su brújula espera.

Ese contraste explica por qué el avance funciona mejor que un simple aumento de poder. Tanjiro no vence la ventaja de Akaza intentando superarlo únicamente en fuerza. Encuentra una forma de percibir mejor al demonio y de volverse mucho más difícil de percibir para él.
¿Qué relación tiene con Yoriichi y Tanjuro?

El Mundo Transparente conecta el crecimiento de Tanjiro con enseñanzas que estaban presentes en su familia mucho antes de que pudiera entenderlas. Tanjuro demuestra una percepción y un control corporal extraordinarios pese a su fragilidad física, mientras que Yoriichi representa el nivel más extremo de este tipo de percepción.

Eso refuerza una idea recurrente en Demon Slayer: algunos de los avances más importantes de Tanjiro no aparecen de la nada. Son el resultado de comprender finalmente recuerdos, movimientos y enseñanzas que llevaba años observando sin conocer su verdadero significado.
La forma más sencilla de entender el Mundo Transparente

El Mundo Transparente es percepción de combate llevada a un nivel extraordinario. Permite observar las señales físicas internas que preceden al movimiento de un rival y utilizar esa información para predecir lo que hará a continuación. Tanjiro lo alcanza contra Akaza, mientras que el Estado Desinteresado cumple otra función: ocultar el espíritu de lucha que Akaza puede detectar.

En resumen: las Respiraciones determinan cómo combate un cazador, la Marca potencia el cuerpo, el Mundo Transparente potencia la percepción y el Estado Desinteresado reduce la intención combativa detectable. Castillo Infinito reúne estos conceptos en una misma pelea, pero cada uno tiene un papel diferente.

faq.answer: Es un estado avanzado de percepción que permite observar con enorme precisión el cuerpo y los movimientos de un rival, incluyendo señales físicas que ayudan a anticipar sus ataques.
faq.question: ¿Qué es el Mundo Transparente en Demon Slayer?

faq.answer: No. El Mundo Transparente mejora la percepción del oponente, mientras que el Estado Desinteresado suprime el espíritu de lucha y la intención que un rival como Akaza puede detectar.
faq.question: ¿El Mundo Transparente y el Estado Desinteresado son lo mismo?

faq.answer: No. Es una capacidad perceptiva independiente. Otros espadachines que no utilizan la Respiración del Sol también pueden acceder a ella.
faq.question: ¿El Mundo Transparente es parte de la Respiración del Sol?

faq.answer: Tanjiro es el ejemplo principal en Castillo Infinito, pero el manga también muestra o confirma a otros usuarios excepcionales, entre ellos Yoriichi, Gyomei, Muichiro y Obanai.

children.text: The
Kagurabachi
anime will officially begin
broadcasting and streaming in April 2027
. The adaptation of Takeru Hokazono’s Weekly Shonen Jump manga is being produced by
Cypic
, with
Tetsuya Takeuchi
directing and
Keigo Sasaki
handling character design. Crunchyroll has also confirmed that it will simulcast the series beginning in April 2027 alongside the Japanese broadcast.
An exact premiere day has
not
been announced yet. For now, April 2027 is the official release window, and any more specific date circulating online should be treated as unconfirmed until the production committee announces it.

The anime is already well beyond the rumor stage: a teaser visual and trailer have been released, principal cast members have been announced, and a world tour is previewing the opening 20 minutes of Episode 1 ahead of the television premiere.
Kagurabachi Anime Release Date: Quick Answer
Here is the confirmed information at a glance:
Anime adaptation:
Confirmed
Release window:
April 2027
Exact premiere date:
Not yet announced
Format:
TV anime
Animation production:
Cypic
Director:
Tetsuya Takeuchi
Character design:
Keigo Sasaki
Chihiro Rokuhira:
Voiced by Taihi Kimura
Kunishige Rokuhira:
Voiced by Tomokazu Seki
Togo Shiba:
Voiced by Katsuyuki Konishi
Streaming:
Crunchyroll simulcast confirmed
Source material:
Takeru Hokazono’s
Weekly Shonen Jump
manga
The key distinction is simple:
April 2027 is confirmed; a specific day is not.
Is the Kagurabachi Anime Officially Confirmed?
Yes.
Kagurabachi
is officially receiving a television anime adaptation.
The production was formally announced on April 27, 2026. The official anime website and CyberAgent both confirmed that broadcasting and streaming will begin in April 2027.
This matters because
Kagurabachi

had been surrounded by adaptation reports and speculation before the formal reveal. Those older reports are no longer the best source for the project’s status. The official announcement now gives us the production studio, director, character designer, initial cast and release month directly from the production side.
When Exactly Does the Kagurabachi Anime Come Out?
As of August 2026, the official release information is
April 2027
. No exact day has been announced.

That means it would be premature to label the anime with a specific April premiere date. Japanese television scheduling, episode timing and detailed international availability can be announced closer to broadcast.

For readers tracking the release, the next important update is an exact premiere date rather than another prediction about the season. Once the production committee confirms that date, this page should be updated accordingly.
Where Will Kagurabachi Stream?
Crunchyroll has officially confirmed a
simulcast beginning in April 2027 alongside the Japanese broadcast

That is one of the most important updates since the anime’s initial reveal because it answers the main international streaming question well ahead of release. The official announcement did not, however, provide every territory-specific detail, language option or exact episode release time.
Those details should remain listed as unknown until Crunchyroll or the anime’s official channels provide them.
Who Is Animating Kagurabachi?
The anime is being produced by
Cypic
, an animation studio under the CyberAgent group. The official announcement identifies Cypic with work including
Umamusume: Cinderella Gray
and
The Summer Hikaru Died
This is worth clarifying because earlier adaptation reports frequently used the Cygames Pictures name. The official 2026 materials identify
Cypic
as the animation production studio, so that is the name readers should use for the confirmed production.
For
Kagurabachi

, the studio faces an unusually clear visual challenge. Hokazono’s manga relies heavily on sharp silhouettes, black-heavy compositions, controlled stillness and explosive sword action. A successful adaptation will need more than fluid movement; it will need direction that preserves the manga’s contrast between restrained tension and sudden violence.
Readers interested in how sword-focused protagonists compare across anime can also see our
Strongest Anime Swordsmen of All Time
ranking.
That makes the announced director especially relevant.
Who Is Directing the Kagurabachi Anime?
Tetsuya Takeuchi
is directing the television anime.
The official announcement highlights his action-animation work on
Sword Art Online II
and battle-scene storyboard, episode direction and animation work on
Heavenly Delusion
. Those credits make sense for a series in which the readability and impact of sword combat will be central to the adaptation.
Keigo Sasaki
is handling character design. The official announcement cites his character-design work on
Blue Exorcist
and
The Seven Deadly Sins
The production committee is led by
Shochiku and CyberAgent

It is still too early to judge the finished series from staff names alone. What the announced team does tell us is that action staging and character animation appear to be important parts of the production’s creative foundation. For a broader look at what makes animated combat memorable, our
Best Anime Fights of All Time
feature explores standout battles across the medium.
Who Voices Chihiro Rokuhira?
Taihi Kimura
voices protagonist Chihiro Rokuhira.

Chihiro is the son of renowned swordsmith Kunishige Rokuhira. After an attack by the mysterious sorcerer organization known as the Hishaku destroys his former life and six Enchanted Blades are stolen, Chihiro takes up
Enten
, the seventh blade left by his father, and begins pursuing revenge.
The official anime site describes him as a quiet young man traveling to avenge his father and recover the six stolen Enchanted Blades.
The cast announced so far also includes
Tomokazu Seki as Kunishige Rokuhira
and
Katsuyuki Konishi as Togo Shiba
More cast announcements are expected as promotion continues, but unannounced roles should not be assigned based on speculation or fan casting.
Is There a Kagurabachi Anime Trailer?
Yes. The first official teaser trailer and teaser visual were released with the anime announcement in April 2026.

The teaser is more useful than a simple confirmation video because it gives viewers an early sense of how Cypic is translating the manga’s visual identity into motion. The production now has official promotional material rather than concept-only announcements.

Still, a teaser should not be mistaken for a complete representation of weekly production quality. A fuller promotional video closer to April 2027 will provide a better indication of the anime’s pacing, voice performances, music and extended action direction.
Kagurabachi Episode 1 Is Getting an Early World Tour Preview
The production has announced a
Kagurabachi Anime World Tour
featuring the first 20 minutes of Episode 1 at anime events around the world ahead of the April 2027 broadcast.

The tour is particularly notable because it gives selected audiences a substantial look at the premiere rather than a conventional short trailer. The official announcement also says the tour finale in Japan will feature the first complete screening of Episode 1.
This does
not
change the television release date. The public broadcast and streaming launch remains scheduled for April 2027. The world-tour screenings are advance promotional events.
That distinction is important for searchers who encounter reports that Episode 1 is being shown before 2027: an event preview is not the same thing as the regular anime premiere.
What Is the Kagurabachi Anime About?
Kagurabachi
follows
Chihiro Rokuhira
, a young man who trained under his father, Kunishige, a celebrated swordsmith.
Their life is destroyed when the Hishaku attacks. Six immensely powerful
Enchanted Blades
are stolen, and Chihiro is left with Enten, the seventh blade forged by his father. He sets out to avenge Kunishige and recover the stolen weapons.

That premise develops into more than a straightforward revenge story. The manga combines sword combat and sorcery with criminal organizations, competing interests surrounding the Enchanted Blades and questions about what these weapons mean to the people who wield, inherit and pursue them.
If that combination of supernatural combat and a compact manga foundation interests you, our analysis of
Why Black Torch Works Better as an Anime
examines another action manga whose structure lends itself particularly well to animation.
For the anime, the opening material has a strong advantage: Chihiro’s objective is immediately understandable, while the world can expand naturally around his pursuit of the blades.
What Will Kagurabachi Season 1 Cover?
The production committee has
not officially announced the anime’s episode count or complete manga coverage

For that reason, assigning a definitive endpoint to Season 1 would be speculation. The early manga gives the adaptation several natural story movements, but how far the television series travels will depend on its episode order and adaptation pace.

The safer expectation is that the anime will begin from Chihiro’s introduction and establish the Enchanted Blades, Hishaku and the central revenge narrative. Exactly which later arc forms the season finale remains unconfirmed.

This is an area where release-date articles often become misleading: a plausible manga stopping point can quickly be repeated as though it were announced production information. Until an episode count or official story breakdown appears, AnimeSparks will keep that distinction clear.
Why Kagurabachi’s Anime Adaptation Matters
Kagurabachi
reached anime adaptation status unusually quickly for a modern Weekly Shonen Jump title, but speed alone is not what makes the project interesting.

The manga has an identity that depends heavily on visual execution. Hokazono frequently uses cinematic composition, negative space and sudden bursts of movement to make sword attacks feel decisive. The Enchanted Blades also create effects that can become visually spectacular without abandoning the story’s darker atmosphere.

That gives Cypic an opportunity and a risk. An adaptation that merely adds movement could miss what makes the panels effective. One that understands timing, framing and silence could make the transition to animation feel natural.

The announced creative staff and early promotional material make the production worth watching, but the responsible assessment remains the same: the finished episodes will determine whether the anime captures the manga’s particular visual rhythm.
What Is Still Unknown About the Kagurabachi Anime?
Several important details remain unconfirmed even though the April 2027 window is official.
The exact April 2027 premiere day
The total episode count
The complete broadcast schedule
Full international territory and language details
The complete cast
The exact manga endpoint for the first season
Opening and ending theme information

None of these should be filled with estimates and presented as fact. The official website is actively releasing new character and distribution information, so several of these gaps are likely to close as the premiere approaches.
Frequently Asked Questions

Kagurabachi
TV anime is officially scheduled to begin broadcasting and streaming in
April 2027
. An exact premiere day has not yet been announced.

is handling animation production. Shochiku and CyberAgent are the production committee leads.

Crunchyroll has officially confirmed that it will simulcast
Kagurabachi
beginning in April 2027 alongside the Japanese broadcast. More detailed regional information has not yet been announced.
Who voices Chihiro in Kagurabachi?
Taihi Kimura
voices Chihiro Rokuhira. Tomokazu Seki voices Kunishige Rokuhira, and Katsuyuki Konishi voices Togo Shiba.
How many episodes will Kagurabachi have?

The episode count has not been officially announced as of August 2026. Any specific episode total currently circulating should be treated as unconfirmed unless it comes from the production’s official channels.
Final Update
The answer is now official:
the Kagurabachi anime comes out in April 2027
, with Crunchyroll simulcasting the series alongside its Japanese broadcast.

Cypic is producing the adaptation under director Tetsuya Takeuchi, with Keigo Sasaki as character designer. Taihi Kimura leads the announced cast as Chihiro Rokuhira, joined by Tomokazu Seki as Kunishige and Katsuyuki Konishi as Shiba. A teaser is already available, and the production is taking the opening 20 minutes of Episode 1 on a world tour before the television launch.
The biggest missing release detail is now the
exact April premiere date
. Until that is officially announced, April 2027 is the most precise confirmed answer—not a rumored day or an estimated schedule.

children.text: One Piece Episode 1180 airs on September 27, 2026 in Japan and closes the anime’s 2026 Elbaph broadcast run. The episode is titled “Elbaph in Despair - Diabolical Covenant, ‘Domi Reversi’,” and its official preview puts Imu’s terrifying new technique at the center of the finale.

The important scheduling detail is that Episode 1180 is the final One Piece TV episode of 2026. The Elbaph story itself is not ending. The anime is entering another planned break under Toei Animation’s revised production model, with the next phase expected in 2027. An exact 2027 return date has not been announced.
When does One Piece Episode 1180 release?

Episode 1180 is scheduled for Sunday, September 27, 2026 in Japan. The Japanese television broadcast airs on Fuji TV and affiliated stations in the anime’s current Sunday-night slot. International availability varies by region and platform, so viewers should check their local Crunchyroll or other licensed service schedule.

The episode’s title translates to “Elbaph in Despair - Diabolical Covenant, ‘Domi Reversi’.” The preview shows the crisis on Elbaph escalating around Imu, Gunko and the giants rather than resolving the island’s larger conflict.
Is Episode 1180 the end of the Elbaph arc?

No. Episode 1180 is the end of One Piece’s 2026 anime run, not the end of the full Elbaph arc. The manga’s Elbaph story continues beyond the material covered by this episode, and the television adaptation is pausing before continuing the arc in a later production block.

That distinction is especially important because older One Piece viewing habits make a season-style finale easy to misread. For most of its history, the anime aired almost continuously. Its newer production plan deliberately creates longer breaks, so a yearly finale can arrive while the current manga arc is still being adapted.
Why is One Piece going on hiatus again?

The break follows the production strategy announced for the anime’s post-Egghead era. One Piece now targets a maximum of 26 television episodes per year rather than maintaining an uninterrupted weekly schedule across nearly the entire calendar.

The goal is to give the production more time and create a healthier gap between the anime and Eiichiro Oda’s manga. It also changes how viewers should think about One Piece releases: the series can now have defined broadcast blocks and off-season periods without those pauses meaning the anime has been cancelled or that an arc has concluded.

AnimeSparks previously covered the three-month pause that followed Episode 1155. That break ended when Elbaph began on April 5, 2026. Episode 1180 now marks the next major stopping point in this newer schedule.
What is Domi Reversi in Episode 1180?

The official Episode 1180 preview identifies Domi Reversi as the major new threat surrounding Imu and the giants. The preview deliberately emphasizes its frightening effect without explaining every rule behind the ability.

For anime-only viewers, that is the safest place to stop before the episode airs. Manga explanations can reveal consequences and mechanics that the television adaptation has not yet shown. This article therefore treats Domi Reversi as an anime-preview development rather than importing later manga information into the episode guide.
What happened before Episode 1180?

The latest Elbaph episodes pushed the conflict far beyond the Straw Hats simply exploring the giants’ homeland. The Knights of God have become an immediate threat, Scopper Gaban has been drawn into the fighting, and Imu’s influence over Gunko has transformed the scale of the crisis.

Episode 1179 left Elbaph in an increasingly dangerous position after Gaban’s confrontation with Sommers and the developments involving Gunko. The Episode 1180 preview shifts attention to Imu’s next move and the effect Domi Reversi has on the giants.

That makes the 2026 finale less like a conventional arc conclusion and more like a deliberate cliffhanger. Viewers should expect the broadcast block to stop while major Elbaph conflicts remain unresolved.
When will the One Piece anime return in 2027?

There is no confirmed return date yet. The anime is expected to continue in 2027 under the same broader production model, but Toei Animation has not announced the exact month or episode date for the next Elbaph broadcast block.

Any specific January, April or other 2027 date circulating before an official announcement should therefore be treated as speculation. The most useful confirmed information right now is simply that Episode 1180 ends the 2026 run and the Elbaph adaptation still has more story to cover.
How the new One Piece annual schedule works

One Piece’s move toward a maximum of 26 episodes per year is one of the biggest structural changes in the anime’s long history. Instead of expecting a new episode almost every week indefinitely, viewers should now expect periods of active broadcasting followed by planned production breaks.

The 2026 schedule demonstrates what that can look like. After the Egghead-era hiatus, Elbaph began in April and ran through September. The September 27 finale then creates another off-season period before the anime’s 2027 continuation.

The approach also gives the manga more breathing room. A continuously weekly anime can close the distance to its source material quickly, forcing adaptation teams to slow pacing, add anime-original material or schedule interruptions. Fewer annual episodes create another way to manage that gap.
Where does Episode 1180 fit in the Elbaph story?

Elbaph began as the long-awaited arrival at the homeland of the giants, a location One Piece had foreshadowed for decades through characters such as Dorry and Brogy. The arc quickly expanded into a Final Saga storyline involving Loki, the Knights of God, the World Government and deeper questions about the history of the One Piece world.

Those historical threads connect naturally to mysteries AnimeSparks has covered separately, including the Void Century and the Will of D. Elbaph is increasingly important because the Straw Hats are not simply visiting another island. The arc is bringing present-day conflict into contact with the inherited history that has shaped the entire series.
What happens after Episode 1180?
The immediate answer is a wait. Episode 1180 closes the 2026 television run, while the remaining Elbaph material will continue when the anime returns.

The franchise will still be active during the gap. One Piece has other major projects in development, including the previously announced God Valley film for 2027. Those projects should not be confused with the next regular Elbaph episode, however. A movie release and the TV anime’s return are separate schedule questions.
Until Toei Animation publishes the next television date, there is no reliable reason to assign Episode 1181 or the next broadcast block a specific 2027 premiere.
The short answer

One Piece Episode 1180 releases September 27, 2026 in Japan and serves as the anime’s final television episode of the year. It is not the end of the Elbaph arc. The story will continue after another production break, but the exact 2027 return date has not been announced.

The finale centers on Imu, the giants and the newly highlighted Domi Reversi threat. For viewers following the anime only, the safest expectation is a major Elbaph cliffhanger followed by a wait for Toei Animation’s official 2027 schedule.

children.text: Made in Abyss (2017) weaponizes the contrast between its childlike Studio Ghibli-inspired art style and its brutal body horror to create uniquely unsettling storytelling. The series follows children Riko and Reg descending into a mysterious pit called the Abyss, where cute character designs collide with graphic violence, psychological trauma, and existential dread. The beauty—hand-painted backgrounds, whimsical creatures, wonder-filled exploration—makes the horror hit harder. When characters suffer horrific injuries or transformations, the contrast between what you see (adorable kids) and what happens to them (dismemberment, body horror, death) creates cognitive dissonance that haunts viewers long after watching. This isn't accidental—it's the core of what makes Made in Abyss both a masterpiece and deeply controversial.

Since its 2017 release, Made in Abyss has maintained an 8.6+ rating on MyAnimeList and won the 2018 Anime of the Year award at Crunchyroll, proving its impact despite—or because of—its controversial content.
The Deceptive First Impression

Made in Abyss draws viewers in with delicate, storybook visuals and a childlike sense of wonder. The first episodes feel cozy—quirky interactions, whimsical creature designs, and soft character expressions that give off a sense of safety and innocence.

The chibi-style animation reminds viewers of Studio Ghibli's warmest works. Hand-painted backgrounds rival theatrical productions. Sunlight hits the town of Orth beautifully, rivers weave through districts, and everything looks meticulously crafted.
Then episode 10 happens.
When the Mask Falls Off

What appears at first to be a cutesy adventure story evolves into a claustrophobic, disturbing fable of single-minded determination and a desperate struggle against overwhelming odds that portrays both brutal violence and severe bodily mutilation involving children.

The tonal shift doesn't arrive gradually. It lands with disturbing force—sudden violence, brutal injuries, psychological trauma, and body horror creep into the narrative, shattering any expectation of a fun adventure.
Similar to
how Evangelion uses mecha to explore depression
, Made in Abyss uses its genre trappings (adventure anime) to smuggle in much darker themes about human cost and sacrifice.
The Studio Ghibli Aesthetic Hiding Cosmic Horror

The comparison to Studio Ghibli isn't superficial. Made in Abyss deliberately evokes that aesthetic—the organic, curvilinear art style, the fantasy environments, the attention to environmental detail that makes worlds feel lived-in.
But where Ghibli uses that style to create comfort and wonder, Made in Abyss uses it as camouflage.
Art Style as Weapon
The art isn't just beautiful—it's strategically beautiful. The cuter the characters look, the more disturbing it becomes when terrible things happen to them.

The Puni Plush aesthetic can be misleading. Made in Abyss is in fact a full-throated Cosmic Horror Story with a caliber of body horror and ultra-violence comparable to some of anime's most uncompromising dark fantasy.

This creates cognitive dissonance. Your brain sees adorable children with big eyes and soft features. Then those same children suffer injuries depicted in agonizing, unflinching detail—bones breaking, flesh tearing, bodies transforming into something unrecognizable.
The contrast makes both elements stronger. The beauty emphasizes the horror. The horror makes the beauty feel fragile, temporary, a thin veneer over something monstrous.
The Abyss Itself: Beauty That Kills
The Abyss is the series' central metaphor—a massive, mysterious pit filled with ancient relics, strange creatures, and otherworldly beauty that hides its grim nature.

No one knows how deep it goes or how it came to be. It's an Eldritch Location that causes phenomena by sheer proximity. Time moves strangely in the depths. Trying to ascend causes life-threatening symptoms called "the Curse."
The Descent as Metaphor

Going into the Abyss is a one-way journey. Each layer down increases danger. The Curse ensures that returning becomes progressively impossible—mild nausea at shallow depths, intense pain deeper, hallucinations deeper still, and eventually death or transformation into something no longer human.
This "no going back" motif solidifies the horror. You're stuck in your pursuit, trapped in Dante's Inferno's downward spiral with no escape route.
This connects to
how Mushishi shows problems that can't be fixed
—some journeys don't have happy endings, some costs can't be undone.
When Body Horror Happens to Children
The series' most controversial aspect is its willingness to depict graphic violence and body horror involving child characters.
The Poison Scene That Changes Everything

Episode 10 features Riko being poisoned by an Orb Piercer. The poison works fast—her hand balloons grotesquely, blood pours from her eyes and ears. To save her life, Reg must break her arm with a rock, then amputate it while she screams in agony.

The scene is brutal, extended, and unflinching. Smashing, screaming, and shredding fill the soundscape with disturbing vibes. It's rough and ugly in ways that would benefit from leaving elements implied rather than displayed.

But that's the point. Made in Abyss refuses to look away. The series argues that if you're going to show children in danger, you have to show the actual consequences—not sanitized action-hero injuries that heal by next episode.
This parallels
the dark side of competition shown in 100 Meters anime
—both series refuse to prettify suffering.
Bondrewd: The Monster Who Loves
The character who embodies Made in Abyss's thematic horror is Bondrewd, a White Whistle explorer who conducts human experimentation in the Abyss's depths.
He's polite, articulate, even gentle in manner. He seems like a stand-up character. But he's responsible for atrocities carried out under the guise of progress and paternal care.
The Mitty and Nanachi Tragedy
Bondrewd tells two children—Mitty and Nanachi—that he'll send them deep into the Abyss then bring them back up to study the Curse's effects.

When they ascend, Mitty takes the full force of the Curse. Her body transforms into a blob-like creature in constant pain, unable to die, screaming as Nanachi is forced to watch helplessly. Bondrewd then experiments on Mitty's immortal body, destroying and regenerating her organs repeatedly.
The horror isn't just the body horror—it's that Bondrewd genuinely believes his work is righteous. He's the most memorable villain in recent memory, in the worst way.
Despite the horror of his actions, he genuinely believes that his work is for progress, even as it destroys countless lives. The series questions whether intent matters when the outcome is monstrous.
The Curse of the Abyss: Consequences That Matter
Unlike most adventure anime where injuries heal conveniently, Made in Abyss enforces permanent consequences through the Curse system.
How the Curse Works
Each layer of the Abyss has a "Curse"—symptoms that occur when ascending:
Layer 1:
Mild dizziness and nausea
Layer 2:
Heavy nausea, headache, numbness
Layer 3:
Vertigo, hallucinations, balance loss
Layer 4:
Intense pain throughout body, bleeding from every orifice
Layer 5:
Complete sensory deprivation, self-harm, loss of humanity
Layer 6:
Death or loss of humanity/transformation into something monstrous
This creates constant dread. Every step deeper makes returning more impossible. Characters can't just decide to leave—physics itself prevents escape.
The Curse turns adventure into trap. Similar to
why Monster feels more terrifying than horror anime
, the horror comes from inevitability, not jump scares.
Why the Beauty Makes the Horror Worse

The series maintains visual beauty throughout its darkest moments. Even in the deepest, most dangerous layers, the Abyss remains stunning. Bioluminescent creatures glow softly. Underground ecosystems burst with color. Ancient ruins inspire awe.

When Reg and Riko share quiet moments discovering new creatures, when they laugh together despite everything, when they create temporary safety in hostile territory—these moments make the horror that follows unbearable.
You care about these characters. You want them to be okay. The series gives you reasons to hope, then systematically destroys that hope in ways that feel earned, not exploitative.
For viewers seeking similar tonal whiplash,
10 underrated anime you probably missed
includes other series that balance beauty with darkness.
The Music That Shouldn't Work But Does
Composer Kevin Penkin created a soundtrack that matches the visual contrast—beautiful, sometimes playful orchestration accompanying horrific scenes.
The song "Underground River" begins slow and quiet, builds to sharp and blaring intensity, then mellows out. It contains meaningful lyrics highlighting themes of descent and discovery.
"Hanezeve Caradhina" plays during tragic moments with haunting vocals that sound both ancient and alien. The music treats the Abyss as sacred, not evil—a place of wonder that happens to kill people.
This creates emotional whiplash that reinforces the series' core tension: beauty and horror aren't opposites here. They're the same thing.
Who Should (and Shouldn't) Watch This
Watch If You:
Appreciate anime that takes creative risks
Can handle graphic content if it serves thematic purpose
Enjoyed other "cute exterior, dark interior" series like Madoka Magica
Want fantasy adventure that respects consequences
Can separate art style from content maturity
Skip If You:
Can't handle body horror or child endangerment
Prefer sanitized adventure stories
Need happy resolutions to justify dark content
Are sensitive to graphic depictions of suffering
Expect art style to indicate content rating
This connects to
how Chainsaw Man feels wrong on purpose
—discomfort can be intentional artistic choice.
What Made in Abyss Actually Achieves

The series succeeds at something rare: making beauty and horror inseparable. Most anime separate them—beautiful moments provide relief, horrific moments create contrast. Made in Abyss refuses this separation.

Despite its heavy themes, the series maintains delicate balance through pacing that alternates between wonder, tension, and horror—preventing darker elements from becoming overwhelming while never sanitizing consequences.

Nearly a decade after its 2017 premiere, Made in Abyss remains both celebrated and controversial. Its refusal to look away from the costs of adventure created something that haunts viewers in ways typical horror anime can't achieve.
Because when horror wears the face of wonder, you can never look at wonder the same way again.

faq.answer: The series is controversial because it depicts extreme suffering involving children and includes scenes that some viewers consider uncomfortable or unnecessary. Despite this, it is widely praised for its storytelling, worldbuilding, and emotional depth.
faq.question: Why is Made in Abyss considered controversial?

faq.answer: Yes, though it doesn’t look like one at first. Made in Abyss blends fantasy adventure with cosmic and psychological horror, using beauty and innocence to amplify the impact of its darker themes.

faq.answer: The story focuses more on consequences and sacrifice than traditional happy resolutions. While it contains emotional moments of connection, it does not soften the cost of descending into the Abyss.

children.text: Some anime entertain. Others inspire. But March Comes in Like a Lion (3-gatsu no Lion) does something rarer—it heals. This 2016 masterpiece from Studio Shaft doesn't just depict depression; it understands it with a precision that's frequently discussed in mental health circles for its clinical accuracy.
If you've ever felt like you're drowning while everyone around you seems fine, this anime will see you—really see you—in ways few pieces of media ever can.
Why It Feels Like Sitting in a Therapist's Office

Unlike most anime that tackle mental health, March Comes in Like a Lion never names Rei Kiriyama's condition. There's no dramatic diagnosis scene. Instead, the series trusts viewers to recognize depression through lived experience.
The result? One of the most accurate depictions of depression in animation history.
The Visual Language of Depression
Studio Shaft's signature style becomes perfect for portraying mental illness:
Water metaphors
- Rei describes feeling like he's drowning, with imagery of sinking, struggling to breathe, and blue bubbles floating upward representing moments he can't reach the surface.
Color desaturation
- Scenes drain to black-and-white when depression overwhelms him, contrasting sharply with warm, saturated colors of the Kawamoto household.
Physical pressure
- Immense weight crushing him, visualized through distorted perspectives and claustrophobic framing.
Empty spaces

- His apartment contains only bare essentials—futon, instant ramen cups, shogi books scattered on floors. The emptiness itself becomes a character, showing how depression strips away not just motivation but the very texture of living.
These aren't artistic flourishes for drama. They're frighteningly accurate visualizations of how depression actually feels from the inside.
Rei Kiriyama: The Most Relatable Depressed Protagonist

Seventeen-year-old Rei is a professional shogi player living alone in Tokyo. On paper, he's successful—one of only five people who became professional players in middle school. He earns enough to support himself.
So why does he wake up every morning with no emotion, mechanically going through routines, feeling like a monster?
Trauma Layered on Trauma
Rei lost his biological family in a car accident. Relatives didn't want him. His adoptive father took him in for his shogi talent, and adoptive siblings resented him for it.
Shogi wasn't Rei's dream—it was his survival mechanism. The game gave him value when nothing else mattered. Now it defines his entire existence, and he doesn't know who he is without it.

This origin makes Rei's depression feel earned rather than melodramatic. His mental state makes complete sense given his circumstances. He's not "crazy"—he's responding rationally to irrational situations.
The Symptoms No One Talks About
March doesn't just show sadness. It shows:
Anhedonia
- Rei goes days without eating or drinking. He knows he should care, but can't make himself feel hungry.
Social paralysis
- Words get stuck even when he wants to speak. This portrayal of social anxiety captures the physical sensation of words refusing to come out.
Cognitive distortions
- When peers offer encouragement, Rei hears insults. Depression distorts reality.
Self-isolation
- He actively avoids connection, declining invitations, eating lunch alone on roofs.
Physical manifestation
- Depression makes Rei physically weak. He locks himself in his room for days until he can barely stumble to a convenience store.
These are textbook DSM-5 symptoms of major depressive disorder presented with clinical accuracy.
The Kawamoto Sisters: Found Family as Treatment
If Rei represents depression, the Kawamoto sisters represent recovery—not cure, but slow, messy learning to live again.

Akari (eldest), Hinata (middle schooler), and Momo (energetic child) live with their grandfather who runs a traditional wagashi shop. They've also lost family—mother, grandmother, father. But they've processed grief differently, creating a warm household radiating comfort.
How the Kawamotos Actually Help
The sisters don't "fix" Rei. They don't give inspirational speeches. Instead, they offer consistent, unconditional presence:
They feed him
- Knowing he doesn't cook, they regularly invite him for dinner. Food becomes love language.
They don't demand explanations
- When Rei looks terrible, they don't interrogate. They just make space.
This acceptance mirrors healthy adult relationships rarely shown in anime
They need him too
- Rei helps with chores, babysits Momo, supports Hinata. Being needed gives purpose beyond shogi.
They respect his pace
- Recovery isn't linear. Sometimes Rei withdraws. The sisters don't guilt him—they just leave the door open.
This mirrors actual therapeutic relationships. Real healing happens through consistent small acts of care.
The Shogi Metaphor: Life as Strategy
Shogi (Japanese chess) isn't just Rei's profession—it's the perfect metaphor for depression and recovery.
Captured Pieces Can Return

In shogi, captured pieces can be brought back into play on your side. This becomes symbolic: nothing Rei lost is permanently gone. Relationships can rebuild. Purpose can be rediscovered. Even what feels destroyed can return in new forms.
The shogi world provides structure when Rei's internal world feels chaotic. It's both his coping mechanism and his slow path to healing.
Studio Shaft's Visual Therapy
Director Akiyuki Shinbo uses their experimental style for emotional authenticity rather than stylistic flex.
The Drowning Imagery
Water appears constantly—blue bubbles floating upward while Rei sinks, rain pounding windows.
This visual metaphor rivals Neon Genesis Evangelion's psychological symbolism
Episode titles reference this: "Black River," "Torrent," "What Lies on the Opposite Shore."
The Warmth/Cold Contrast
The Kawamoto home uses warm watercolors, pastels, soft pencil-drawn aesthetics. Everything feels handmade, cozy, safe.
Rei's apartment and depressive episodes use harsh blacks, whites, geometric lines, cold palettes. Visual language tells you instantly where Rei's mental state stands.
The Hinata Bullying Arc: Trauma Beyond Rei
Season 2 shifts focus to Hinata Kawamoto. When she witnesses bullying and speaks up, she becomes the target.
The bullying arc is brutal—not violent, but psychologically devastating. Hinata's classmates ostracize her, spread rumors, get her suspended through false accusations.
Why This Arc Matters
Trauma is universal
- Everyone carries wounds. The Kawamotos lost family. Rei's adoptive sister Kyōko is damaged by her own upbringing.
Even secondary characters reveal hidden pain, similar to Pet Girl of Sakurasou's exploration of inadequacy
Support saves lives
- When Hinata breaks down, Akari, Rei, and her teacher rally around her.
Justice isn't guaranteed
- The bully faces minimal consequences. Sometimes life isn't fair, and healing means accepting that while moving forward.
The arc transforms the series from "anime about one depressed boy" to "anime about how we all struggle, and how community makes survival possible."
Why Mental Health Professionals Discuss This Series
Mental health educators and therapists frequently reference March Comes in Like a Lion in professional and educational contexts:
Destigmatizes mental illness
- Rei isn't "crazy." He's responding to abnormal circumstances.
Shows recovery realistically
- Healing is slow, nonlinear, with setbacks. No magic cure.
Validates silent struggles
- Viewers report feeling seen for the first time.
Models healthy support
- The Kawamotos demonstrate how to help someone without fixing them.

According to the National Institute of Mental Health, approximately 16.1 million American adults experienced major depressive episodes in 2015. That's 6.7% who could directly relate to Rei's experience.
The Power of Small Moments
March doesn't rely on dramatic climaxes. Its power comes from tiny moments:
Rei accepting dinner invitation even though he wants to isolate
Hinata asking if he's eaten today
Rei buying snacks for Momo
Akari wordlessly making tea when he can't speak
These small gestures carry the series' weight. Not everything needs fixing; sometimes presence is enough.
What Makes It Different
Many anime tackle depression: Your Lie in April, A Silent Voice, Evangelion. March stands apart:
No romanticization
- Depression isn't beautiful. It's exhausting and ugly.
No quick fixes
- By series end, Rei's improving but still struggling.
Multiple perspectives
- It's not just Rei's story.
Hope without toxicity
- Acknowledges "it gets better" while respecting "better" doesn't mean "cured."
March treats mental illness as lived reality requiring patience and compassion, never sensationalizing it for shock value.
Who Should Watch (And Who Shouldn't)
Watch if you:
Struggle with depression, anxiety, loneliness
Want to understand loved ones with mental illness
Appreciate slow, character-driven storytelling
Value visual symbolism
Skip if you:
Need constant action
Find slice-of-life boring
Can't handle mental health depictions
Want escapist entertainment
This demands emotional investment and patience. But for those willing to engage, the payoff is profound.
The Lasting Impact
Viewers report:
Recognizing their own symptoms
Understanding friends'/family struggles better
Seeking therapy after seeing recovery modeled
Feeling less alone
Appreciating small kindnesses more
The series reminds us everyone carries invisible burdens. That person who seems fine might be drowning.
And crucially: recovery is possible, even when it feels impossible.
Real-World Applications & Why "Therapy" Fits

Therapeutic principles translate to real life: build support systems, accept help incrementally, find purpose in small ways, remember healing isn't linear, and understand that community prevents tragedy.

Calling March "therapy" isn't dramatic. It normalizes seeking help, validates experiences by depicting symptoms accurately, models healthy coping, provides hope through gradual improvement, and creates community among viewers sharing struggles.

Real therapy requires professionals. But for a streaming subscription, this anime offers something valuable: knowledge you're not alone, that what you feel is valid, and that healing, while difficult, is possible.
Conclusion: A Gentle Hand in the Dark
March Comes in Like a Lion doesn't solve depression. It doesn't offer easy answers. What it offers is more valuable: companionship.

When you're drowning, knowing someone else felt this way—and survived—matters more than advice. When you can't explain what's wrong, seeing it visualized on screen provides validation words fail to capture.

Rei Kiriyama's journey isn't about becoming happy. It's about learning to live with pain, to accept help, to believe he deserves warmth. It's about understanding that struggling doesn't make you broken.

If you've ever felt like you're going through life's motions without actually living, this anime will meet you where you are. It won't drag you out of darkness. Instead, it'll sit beside you in it, holding a small light, reminding you daylight still exists—even when you can't see it yet.
That's what makes March Comes in Like a Lion therapy in anime form. Not because it fixes anything, but because it understands. And sometimes, being understood is the first step toward healing.

children.text: Solo Leveling: Beyond the System is an officially announced theatrical anime movie that continues Sung Jinwoo's story after Solo Leveling Season 2. Aniplex and Crunchyroll revealed the project at Anime Expo 2026, with A-1 Pictures returning for animation production. No theatrical release date or release window has been announced.
Beyond the System is a movie, not Season 3

The most important distinction is the format. Beyond the System is being promoted as a theatrical continuation, not as Solo Leveling Season 3. It picks up after Season 2, but a direct narrative continuation does not automatically make it the third television season. If a separate Season 3 is planned later, it has not been announced as part of this movie reveal.
Who is making the Solo Leveling movie?

A-1 Pictures is returning after animating the television series. Crunchyroll is co-producing the film alongside Aniplex, Netmarble, D&C Media and Kakao Piccoma. That continuity is important because the television adaptation established a particular visual language for Jinwoo's shadows, dungeon combat and large-scale boss fights that the movie can build on rather than reinvent.

body.alt: Solo Leveling Sung Jinwoo - Awakened Power and Beyond the System

children.text: What story will Beyond the System cover?

The announcement says the movie continues from where Season 2 left off, which places it in the next phase of Jinwoo's journey. The exact adaptation range has not been announced. That means it is reasonable to discuss unresolved threads from the end of Season 2, but not to claim a precise chapter endpoint, runtime or complete arc list until the production publishes a synopsis.

By this stage of Solo Leveling, Jinwoo is no longer simply a weak hunter trying to survive. His power, the origin of the System and the larger forces behind the gates become increasingly connected. A film format gives the anime room to frame the next escalation as a major event, but it also raises questions about how much material can be adapted without compressing the story.
Is the movie coming out in 2027?

There is no official 2027 release window at present. A 2027 date has circulated in secondary reporting and fan discussion, but the announcement from Crunchyroll and Aniplex confirms the movie's production rather than a year. Until the producers publish a date, AnimeSparks will not convert speculation into a release window.
Will Beyond the System stream on Crunchyroll?

Crunchyroll is co-producing the film and already streams the Solo Leveling television anime, but that does not establish a post-theatrical streaming date. Movies often have separate cinema, home-video and streaming windows. A streaming release should only be listed once Crunchyroll gives a specific availability announcement.
What about Solo Leveling Season 3?

The film does not confirm or cancel a later Season 3. It changes the immediate path of the adaptation by moving the next chapter to theaters. Whether the anime returns to television after Beyond the System will depend on future announcements from the production committee.
What remains unknown

The theatrical date, countries receiving a cinema release, runtime, detailed story range, complete staff and cast list, and eventual streaming plan are still unannounced. The confirmed foundation is already substantial: Beyond the System is real, it is a theatrical continuation after Season 2, A-1 Pictures is returning, and Crunchyroll and Aniplex are directly involved.

children.text: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End Season 3 is officially scheduled to begin in October 2027. The new season is titled around the Golden Land arc, and the first teaser visual prominently features Macht of the Golden Land, one of the Seven Sages of Destruction and a character whose history is central to this part of the story.
Frieren Season 3 release date

The official anime site confirms an October 2027 television premiere on the Nippon TV network. An exact day has not yet been announced. That means October 2027 is firm, while specific weekly broadcast times, international simulcast times and dub schedules should remain unconfirmed until the distribution partners publish them.
What is the Golden Land arc?

The Golden Land arc is one of Frieren's most important long-form stories because it turns a seemingly simple demon problem into a study of memory, morality and whether two very different kinds of beings can ever truly understand one another. The conflict centers on Weise, a city transformed into gold, and Macht, the demon responsible for that catastrophe.

body.alt: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End - Sousou no Frieren

children.text: Why Macht matters

Macht is not interesting simply because he is powerful. Frieren has repeatedly shown that demons can imitate human language and behavior without sharing human emotional instincts. Macht pushes that idea further by genuinely trying to understand concepts such as guilt, malice and coexistence. His problem is that wanting to understand humanity does not automatically make him human or safe.

That makes the Golden Land arc especially suited to Frieren's slower style. The story can move between present-day danger and long stretches of remembered history, gradually explaining how Weise fell and why Macht's relationship with the city's people became so complicated.
What Frieren and Denken bring to the arc

Frieren's experience with demons gives her a very different perspective from people who knew Macht personally. Denken also becomes especially important because the Golden Land is tied to his past. Season 3 is therefore not just another stop on Frieren's journey north; it is a collision between an ancient mage's understanding of demons and a human character's memories of a place that was taken from him.
Will Fern and Stark still be important?

Yes, the traveling party remains central even when the arc spends more time on Macht, Denken and historical material. Frieren works because its major arcs still return to the relationships built during the journey. Fern and Stark provide both practical support and the younger perspective that contrasts with Frieren's long memory.
How much will Season 3 adapt?

The production has confirmed the Golden Land arc but has not announced a final episode count or precise manga endpoint. That matters because the arc is dense with flashbacks, tactical magic and philosophical conversations. A rushed adaptation would lose much of what makes the storyline memorable, so the episode count will be one of the most important details to watch for.
What remains unknown

The exact October premiere day, episode count, complete returning staff list, theme songs and international simulcast schedule remain unannounced. The central information is already official: Frieren Season 3 arrives in October 2027, the Golden Land arc is the focus, and Macht is being positioned as one of its defining characters.

children.text: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 is officially in development as the second half of the Culling Game storyline. The official anime site has released a teaser PV and confirmed Takeshi Sato as director for the new season. As of September 11, 2026, no premiere date or broadcast window has been announced.
Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 is officially confirmed

The official announcement identifies Season 4 as the continuation of the Culling Game, specifically its latter half. That clears up an important naming issue: this is not simply an unofficial label fans are using for more Culling Game episodes. The production itself calls the continuation the fourth television season.

The teaser includes major confrontations involving Kinji Hakari and Hajime Kashimo, Maki Zenin, Choso, Yuki Tsukumo, Kenjaku, Yuji Itadori and Megumi Fushiguro. Those images establish the broad direction of the season without giving away a complete episode-by-episode adaptation map.

body.alt: Jujutsu Kaisen Culling Game Arc - Key Visual

children.text: What part of the Culling Game comes next?

Season 4 continues the increasingly fragmented battles and alliances inside the Culling Game. Rather than following one straightforward mission, the arc moves between colonies and characters whose goals overlap only partially. That structure is why the teaser can show several major fights at once without any of them being side stories.

Maki's development, Hakari's confrontation with Kashimo, and the clash involving Choso, Yuki and Kenjaku are especially important because they expand the conflict beyond Yuji and Megumi. The Culling Game is as much about changing the balance of the jujutsu world as it is about accumulating points inside the colonies.
Who is directing Season 4?

Takeshi Sato is confirmed as director for the latter half of the Culling Game. He previously worked on the first half as an episode director and assistant director, so the change does not mean the production is handing the series to someone unfamiliar with the material. The official announcement specifically highlighted his move into the director role.
When will Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 release?

No date has been announced. A teaser PV confirms active production, but a teaser alone cannot establish whether the season belongs to late 2026, 2027 or another window. The next useful official update would be a broadcast season, a dated key visual, theme-song announcement or television scheduling notice.
Will Season 4 finish the manga?

The official material describes Season 4 as the Culling Game's latter half, not as the final season of Jujutsu Kaisen. The manga contains major material beyond the fights highlighted in this teaser. Without an announced episode count or adaptation endpoint, it would be premature to say exactly where Season 4 will stop.
What remains unknown

The premiere date, episode count, streaming schedule, full staff list and exact manga endpoint remain unannounced. What is confirmed is much clearer than before: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 exists, it continues the Culling Game's latter half, a teaser has been released, and Takeshi Sato is directing.
