children.text: The Ramparts of Ice
Season 2 is officially arriving much sooner than many viewers expected. The anime’s official Japanese website confirms that
Season 2 premieres October 1, 2026
, airing every Thursday on 28 TBS network stations in Japan. Netflix has separately confirmed that the second season will premiere worldwide in
October 2026 with new episodes weekly

The announcement came immediately after Season 1’s 14th and final episode, meaning Koyuki Hikawa, Miki Azumi, Minato Amamiya and Yota Hino will return after only a short break. A Season 2 teaser visual and announcement PV have also been released, and both point toward a more emotionally complicated continuation of the four friends’ relationships.
For viewers searching for the release date, there is no speculation necessary:
The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 begins its Japanese broadcast on October 1, 2026 at 11:56 p.m. JST.
Netflix confirms an October global release, although its media page does not currently specify the worldwide premiere day.
The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 Release Date — Quick Answer
Here is what is officially confirmed:
Season:
The Ramparts of Ice
Season 2
Japanese premiere:
October 1, 2026
Japanese airtime:
Thursdays at 11:56 p.m. JST
Broadcaster:
TBS network, 28 stations nationwide
Netflix:
Worldwide in October 2026, with new episodes weekly
Animation studio:
Studio KAI
Original creator:
Kocha Agasawa
Season 2 teaser visual:
Released
Season 2 announcement PV:
Released
The exact Netflix date is the one detail that should be treated carefully. The official Netflix Media Center currently promises
October 2026
, while the Japanese broadcast has the more precise
October 1
date.
Is The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 Officially Confirmed?
Yes. Season 2 was formally announced after the first season’s finale.

The official anime website lists the second season under its broadcast information and confirms the October 1 start. The production also released a Season 2 announcement video on July 3, following the teaser visual revealed alongside the renewal.

That rapid turnaround is notable. Season 1 began its Japanese television run in April 2026 and concluded with Episode 14 on July 2. Season 2 begins just three months later, keeping the story’s emotional momentum intact rather than asking viewers to wait years for the relationships to continue.
When Does The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 Come Out?
In Japan,
October 1, 2026
is the confirmed date.
Episodes will air every Thursday at 11:56 p.m. across TBS’s 28-station network. Netflix’s official media center says Season 2 will premiere worldwide in October and release new episodes weekly.
That means international viewers should expect the series back during the same month as Japan. Until Netflix publishes a day-specific global schedule, however, the safest wording is
October 2026 worldwide on Netflix
, rather than assuming every territory will receive Episode 1 on October 1.
AnimeSparks uses the same distinction between confirmed dates and broader streaming windows in our
Frieren Season 3 release date guide
, where official production information is kept separate from assumptions about international distribution.
What Is The Ramparts of Ice About?
The Ramparts of Ice
adapts Kocha Agasawa’s completed manga about four teenagers struggling to communicate what they actually feel.

Koyuki Hikawa has learned to keep other people at a distance. Her quiet, emotionally guarded life revolves largely around her childhood friend Miki Azumi until Minato Amamiya starts pushing through the boundaries Koyuki has built around herself. Yota Hino, a gentle basketball player, completes the central group.

The setup sounds like a familiar school romance, but the series is less interested in an easy love triangle than in the ways insecurity changes how teenagers interpret one another. Koyuki can look cold when she is actually frightened of hurting people. Miki’s social confidence does not make her emotionally invulnerable. Minato’s lack of distance can be charming and disruptive at the same time. Yota’s kindness does not erase the difficulty of saying what he wants.

That focus puts the series closer to character-driven romances than to pure wish-fulfillment. Readers looking for another anime that treats awkward communication as the substance of romance can also read our
Horimiya review
What Will Season 2 Be About?
The official Season 2 introduction makes the emotional direction clear without giving away every development.

Koyuki and Minato have grown closer and developed feelings that go beyond ordinary friendship. Yota has finally expressed feelings he had carried for a long time toward Miki. Some characters have spoken; others are still keeping their emotions inside. The result is not immediate romantic clarity but
more crossed signals

That is exactly what the Season 2 teaser visual emphasizes. Koyuki, Miki, Minato and Yota appear together, yet their gazes do not meet. The official promotional language describes an uneasy atmosphere surrounding the four characters and asks what will become of the feelings each of them carries.

Season 2 therefore looks less like a reset and more like the emotional consequence of Season 1. The walls have started to crack, but becoming closer creates new ways for these characters to hurt one another.
Why the Season 2 Teaser Visual Matters
The teaser visual is unusually effective because it communicates the sequel’s premise without relying on a dramatic new character or plot twist.
All four central characters are present, but none of them is looking directly at another. For a series about emotional walls, that visual separation says almost everything necessary.

Season 1 was about creating connections. Season 2 appears ready to ask what happens when those connections become complicated by romantic feelings, jealousy, uncertainty and the fear that honesty could change a friendship permanently.
The visual also reinforces why
The Ramparts of Ice

works best as an ensemble. Koyuki may be the central protagonist, but Miki, Minato and Yota are not merely satellites around her. Each has a private interpretation of the group’s relationships, and those interpretations do not always align.
Koyuki and Minato’s Relationship Is Entering a New Stage
Koyuki and Minato are the relationship most obviously positioned to change in Season 2.

Minato’s willingness to approach Koyuki challenged the emotional distance she had spent years maintaining. Their growing closeness is important because it forces Koyuki to confront a problem isolation allowed her to avoid: relationships require vulnerability.

Season 2 begins from a point where their feelings are no longer easily dismissed as casual friendship. That does not mean the story will suddenly become straightforward. If anything, mutual emotional investment gives both characters more to lose.

Koyuki’s instinct is to retreat when she fears misunderstanding or hurting someone. Minato’s instinct is often to close distance. Those opposite responses can create intimacy, but they can also create pressure.
That tension is likely to remain the core of their relationship.
Miki and Yota Could Be Just as Important
The sequel’s official introduction also points directly toward
Yota’s feelings for Miki

Yota has communicated emotions he had held onto for years, which changes the group even if the answer is not immediately simple. Miki’s role is especially important because her outward confidence can make it easy for other characters—and viewers—to underestimate her own insecurities.
A good ensemble romance understands that confession is not the end of emotional complexity. Sometimes saying what you feel makes the next conversation harder because everyone now knows the stakes.
That appears to be the territory Season 2 wants to explore.
Where Will The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 Stream?
Netflix has officially confirmed that
Season 2 will premiere worldwide in October 2026
, with new episodes arriving weekly.

That is the strongest international streaming confirmation currently available. Season 1 also reached viewers through multiple services in Japan, but availability can vary by territory, so Netflix’s worldwide confirmation is the most useful information for international audiences.
The series is a particularly natural fit for Netflix’s growing anime catalog because it is accessible even to viewers who do not normally watch action-heavy anime. AnimeSparks’
Best Anime on Netflix Right Now
guide is another useful starting point for viewers looking for more series on the platform.
Is Studio KAI Returning?
The anime is produced by
Studio KAI
, with the established production credits including director Mankyu, assistant director Teru Ishii, series composition by Yasuhiro Nakanishi and character design by Miki Ogino.

The official anime website continues to list the series’ staff and cast as Season 2 approaches. The production’s short gap between seasons also gives the sequel a strong sense of continuity with the first run rather than presenting it as a distant revival.

Studio KAI’s challenge is not primarily spectacle. The series depends on small expressions, uncomfortable pauses, changes in body language and the contrast between what characters say aloud and what they are thinking.
Those details are essential in a story where a glance—or the refusal to make eye contact—can carry more meaning than a dramatic speech.
Who Is Returning in the Cast?
The main anime cast includes:
Anna Nagase
as Koyuki Hikawa
Fuka Izumi
as Miki Azumi
Shoya Chiba
as Minato Amamiya
Satoshi Inomata
as Yota Hino
Sakura Shinfuku
as Tsukiko Shimojima
Chiaki Kobayashi
as Tsubasa Igarashi
Akari Kito
as Momoka Kuriki
Kakeru Hatano
as Yuki Azumi
The four leads remain the emotional center of the sequel’s promotional material, particularly Koyuki, Miki, Minato and Yota.
Is There a Season 2 Trailer?
Yes, a
Season 2 announcement PV
has been released.

The official anime news page lists the video as released on July 3, one day after the second season and teaser visual were announced. The PV functions as confirmation of the continuation and a bridge from the first season into the October return.

As the premiere approaches, additional promotional material could reveal theme songs, episode previews or more specific streaming information. Those details should be treated as future updates rather than assumed in advance.
How Popular Is The Ramparts of Ice?
The anime is adapting a manga with a substantial audience already behind it.
By 2026, official and industry materials reported more than
190 million cumulative views on LINE Manga
and over
2.8 million copies in circulation
, including digital editions. The original manga ran from January 2020 to April 2022 and is complete.

That completed source material is useful for the anime because the adaptation is not waiting for the manga to generate a future ending. The production has a finished character arc to work from, even though Season 2’s exact adaptation endpoint and episode count have not been publicly specified.
Why The Ramparts of Ice Stands Out Among Romance Anime

body.alt: Koyuki and Minato separated by a glowing ice wall in The Ramparts of Ice anime
body.insertAfterHeading: ## Why The Ramparts of Ice Stands Out Among Romance Anime

children.text: The title itself explains much of the series’ appeal.

Koyuki’s “wall” is not simply shyness. It is a defense mechanism created by the belief that distance is safer than being misunderstood. The story becomes compelling when other characters do not magically fix that insecurity but instead force Koyuki to experience the uncertainty that comes with genuine connection.
That is why the romance works best when it is awkward. These teenagers do not always understand their own feelings, much less communicate them perfectly to someone else.
AnimeSparks has explored a similarly character-focused approach in
How My Dress-Up Darling Redefines Romance in Modern Anime
. The two shows have very different personalities, but both are strongest when romance reveals vulnerability rather than functioning only as a destination.
How Many Episodes Will Season 2 Have?
A definitive Season 2 episode count is not prominently confirmed on the official broadcast page at the time of writing.

Season 1 ran for 14 episodes, but that should not automatically be used to claim that Season 2 will have the same number. Broadcast length, home-video listings or later scheduling information may clarify the total closer to October.
For now, the confirmed information is the October 1 Japanese premiere and weekly Thursday broadcast.
What Is Still Unconfirmed?
Even with an exact Japanese premiere date, a few details still need clarification:
The precise Netflix premiere day in every international territory
The final Season 2 episode count
The exact manga chapters Season 2 will adapt
Any additional cast announcements
Season 2 opening and ending theme details not yet formally announced
The exact ending point of the second season
Those gaps are normal for a sequel still several weeks away. The important difference is that the biggest question—the Japanese release date—has already been answered.
Should You Watch Season 1 Before Season 2?
Absolutely. Season 2 is a direct continuation, not a standalone romantic storyline.

The emotional tension only works if viewers understand why Koyuki keeps people at a distance, how Minato gradually entered her life, what Miki means to Koyuki and why Yota’s feelings change the group dynamic.

The series is built on accumulated misunderstandings and small moments rather than a plot that can be summarized in a few minutes. Skipping Season 1 would remove much of the context that makes the sequel’s uneasy teaser visual meaningful.
For viewers who want more character-driven romance after catching up, AnimeSparks also has a list of
romance anime like Toradora!
, another series where messy teenage communication matters as much as the eventual pairing.
Final Update
The Ramparts of Ice
Season 2 is officially confirmed for
October 1, 2026
on TBS’s 28-station network in Japan, airing every Thursday at 11:56 p.m. JST. Netflix has confirmed a
worldwide October 2026 premiere with weekly episodes

The sequel arrives only three months after Season 1’s finale and continues the increasingly complicated relationships between Koyuki, Miki, Minato and Yota. The Season 2 teaser visual deliberately shows the four characters unable to meet one another’s gaze, suggesting that the emotional walls of the title are far from gone.
The exact Netflix day and Season 2 episode count still need confirmation, but the main release-date question is settled:
The Ramparts of Ice returns in October 2026, with its Japanese broadcast beginning October 1.

children.text: Finishing
Solo Leveling

leaves a very specific itch. You want another series where getting stronger actually feels exciting—where a character walks into a fight that once would have terrified them and you can immediately see how far they have come.
The problem is that simply recommending ten anime with overpowered protagonists misses what makes
Solo Leveling
work. Sung Jinwoo's appeal is not just that he becomes absurdly strong. It is the
progression
: the dungeon raids, visible growth, increasingly dangerous enemies, status systems, lone-wolf aura and the satisfaction of watching the weakest hunter become the person everyone else fears.

So this list is built around different pieces of that experience. Some shows have literal game mechanics. Some have dungeon crawling. Some offer the same overwhelming protagonist fantasy. Others match
Solo Leveling
through escalating battles, dark supernatural worlds or a hero whose growth changes how everyone sees him.
If you're caught up with Jinwoo himself, AnimeSparks also has a guide to
Solo Leveling: Beyond the System
, the theatrical continuation announced after Season 2.
10. Sword Art Online
If the interface, stats and RPG flavor of
Solo Leveling
are what hooked you,
Sword Art Online
remains one of the obvious next stops.

Kirito is trapped with thousands of players inside Aincrad, a virtual-reality MMORPG where dying in the game means dying in the real world. Floors have to be cleared, bosses have to be learned, gear matters, and combat skill determines whether players ever get home.
The comparison with
Solo Leveling

is not exact. Jinwoo's System exists inside a real supernatural world, while SAO begins with a literal game. But both series understand the appeal of translating RPG progression into anime spectacle. Kirito also scratches some of the same lone-wolf protagonist itch, especially during Aincrad.
SAO is inconsistent across its many arcs, but its influence on game-world anime is impossible to ignore. If you want the longer version of that argument, read
why Sword Art Online changed virtual reality anime forever
Watch this if:
you want levels, bosses, game mechanics and a highly capable swordsman at the center.
9. Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon?
Ignore the title for a moment.
DanMachi
is one of the better recommendations for viewers who specifically miss the
dungeon
side of
Solo Leveling

body.alt: Best Anime Like Solo Leveling - Tower of God and Hunter Fantasy Recommendations

children.text: Bell Cranel begins as an inexperienced adventurer entering the enormous Dungeon beneath Orario. He is not secretly the strongest person in the world. He gets hurt, needs allies and spends much of the early story looking painfully small next to elite adventurers.
That is exactly why his growth works.

Like Jinwoo, Bell has an unusual path to rapid improvement, but DanMachi gives the progression more of a classic fantasy-adventure feeling. The Dungeon has floors, monsters and threats that become increasingly hostile the deeper characters go. Later arcs also become considerably darker than the playful title suggests.
The payoff is less about instant domination and more about watching Bell slowly become the adventurer other people once seemed impossibly far above.
Watch this if:
dungeon raids and visible character progression were your favorite parts of
Solo Leveling
8. Kaiju No. 8
Kafka Hibino and Sung Jinwoo begin in very different circumstances, but they share one important quality: both know what it feels like to stand below the people they wanted to become.

Kafka has spent years cleaning up kaiju remains while watching others fight the monsters he once dreamed of facing. Then his body changes, giving him a power that could make him one of humanity's greatest weapons—or mark him as a monster that needs to be eliminated.
Kaiju No. 8

has no leveling System, and Kafka's personality is much warmer and more openly comedic than Jinwoo's. The similarity comes from the pleasure of watching someone dismissed by the existing hierarchy reveal strength that completely changes how that hierarchy sees him.
The Defense Force structure also gives the series rankings, elite fighters and monster threats that can appeal to viewers who enjoyed
Solo Leveling
's Hunter Association and S-Rank ecosystem.
Watch this if:
you liked hunters, rankings, monster threats and the moment everyone realizes the underestimated protagonist is terrifyingly powerful.
7. Jujutsu Kaisen
Jujutsu Kaisen
is the recommendation for viewers who care less about RPG mechanics and more about
Solo Leveling
's supernatural battles.

Yuji Itadori enters a hidden world of curses after swallowing one of Sukuna's fingers. From there, the anime builds an increasingly dangerous hierarchy of sorcerers, cursed spirits, inherited techniques and Domain Expansions.

JJK does not deliver Jinwoo-style solo progression. Its power system is much more distributed across an ensemble, and Yuji is frequently surrounded by people who are more experienced or technically stronger than he is. What it does share is a taste for dangerous missions that can suddenly become catastrophes when an enemy is far beyond the expected level.
The animation is another obvious bridge. If what you want after
Solo Leveling
is simply more modern action anime with fights designed to become events, JJK is difficult to skip.
The next stage is already underway; AnimeSparks has the latest on
Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4: Culling Game Part 2
Watch this if:
the fights, monsters and high-end animation mattered more to you than the game interface.
6. Tower of God
There is an obvious reason
Tower of God
belongs on a post-
Solo Leveling
watchlist: both grew from Korean webtoon culture and became major anime adaptations. But the better reason is their shared obsession with
ascending through a hostile system

Bam enters the Tower looking for Rachel. Each floor brings tests, alliances, betrayals and increasingly strange rules. Progress is physical, social and psychological rather than represented through a visible stat screen.
Where
Solo Leveling
becomes increasingly focused on Jinwoo's overwhelming individual strength,
Tower of God
is much more interested in factions, mysteries and the people controlling the structure everyone is trying to climb.
That makes it a good recommendation for viewers who enjoyed the sense that Jinwoo was operating inside a much larger world whose rules he did not initially understand.
We have a full breakdown of
whether Tower of God is still worth watching in 2026
if you are unsure about committing to it.
Watch this if:
you want Korean-source fantasy, tests, rankings, mysteries and a world built around climbing higher.
5. Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation
This is not the recommendation to pick if all you want is Jinwoo effortlessly deleting monsters.
Mushoku Tensei

is slower, more character-driven and considerably more controversial. Rudeus Greyrat begins a second life in a fantasy world and develops extraordinary magical ability, but the series is interested in the years between major victories: learning languages, traveling, damaging relationships, repairing them and discovering how enormous the world really is.
The connection to
Solo Leveling
is
growth

, not tone. Both protagonists start from positions of profound weakness and eventually operate on a scale that would once have seemed impossible. But Rudeus's progression is tied to an entire second life rather than a rapid System-driven transformation.

It is also worth knowing that the series contains sexual and behavioral material that many viewers find uncomfortable. That should be part of the recommendation rather than buried after someone starts watching.
For readers who enjoy detailed power hierarchies, our guide to
Mushoku Tensei's Seven Great Powers
explains the legendary figures at the top of its world.
Watch this if:
you want another fantasy where becoming powerful feels like a long journey through a much larger world.
4. That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
Rimuru Tempest and Sung Jinwoo share the kind of progression that makes you periodically stop and remember how unimpressive they were at the beginning.

Rimuru starts as a slime with an ability that lets him absorb and analyze other beings. That foundation grows into a huge collection of skills, evolutions and eventually political power. But Tensura's smartest choice is refusing to make combat the only form of progression.
Rimuru builds a nation.

Monsters become citizens. Villages become infrastructure. Alliances, trade and diplomacy start mattering alongside new abilities. The power fantasy therefore expands outward: getting stronger changes not only what Rimuru can defeat but what kind of society he can protect.
It is much warmer and more communal than
Solo Leveling
, which increasingly isolates Jinwoo at the top. But if watching numbers, abilities and status evolve is the addictive part for you, Tensura delivers that satisfaction on a huge scale.
Watch this if:
you want an overpowered protagonist, constant evolution and a progression fantasy that grows into nation-building.
3. The Eminence in Shadow
If the image you have in your head when someone says
Solo Leveling
is Jinwoo walking out of darkness with an army behind him,
The Eminence in Shadow
may be the easiest recommendation on this list.

Cid Kagenou is absurdly powerful. He dresses in black. He commands a secret organization. He loves dramatic entrances. He speaks like a final boss even when nobody around him understands what he is doing.
The difference is that
The Eminence in Shadow
knows how ridiculous this fantasy is.

Cid invents an elaborate conspiracy as part of his role-playing fantasy, only to accidentally describe a conspiracy that actually exists. He thinks he is improvising. His followers think he is an incomprehensible genius. The joke continues because the world takes him far more seriously than he takes the world.
That makes the series a strange but effective follow-up to
Solo Leveling
. It delivers the same kind of overwhelming cool-factor while simultaneously making fun of the desire to look overwhelmingly cool.
AnimeSparks has a full review of
why The Eminence in Shadow works
, including why its parody never prevents the action from landing.
Watch this if:
Shadow Monarch Jinwoo was your favorite version of Jinwoo and you are willing to laugh at the power fantasy while enjoying it.
2. Shangri-La Frontier
Shangri-La Frontier
may be the closest recommendation for people who love the actual
process
of getting better.

Rakuro Hizutome, better known as Sunraku, is not trapped in another world. He is playing a virtual-reality game because he genuinely loves games—especially difficult ones. His experience beating terrible, broken games gives him an unusual skill set when he enters the polished MMO Shangri-La Frontier.
The series understands something crucial about progression fantasy: improvement is more satisfying when the audience understands the challenge.

Boss mechanics matter. Equipment matters. Timing matters. Other players matter. Sunraku can be extremely capable without making every encounter feel predetermined because the game continually introduces problems that require adaptation rather than a bigger attack number.
It lacks
Solo Leveling
's darker supernatural atmosphere, but it captures the excitement of discovering a new ability, entering a dangerous area and realizing a boss is operating on a completely different level.
Watch this if:
leveling, boss fights and the feeling of mastering a system are what made
Solo Leveling
addictive.
1. The Rising of the Shield Hero
For viewers chasing the specific fantasy of
starting at the bottom and forcing the world to reconsider you
The Rising of the Shield Hero
is one of the clearest follow-ups.

Naofumi Iwatani is summoned to another world as one of four Cardinal Heroes and almost immediately finds himself disgraced, isolated and treated with contempt. His Shield also prevents him from fighting like the conventional damage-dealing heroes around him.
So he adapts.

Naofumi learns to exploit what his class can do, builds a party and becomes increasingly difficult for the people who dismissed him to ignore. That underdog-to-powerful trajectory is the strongest link to Jinwoo. Both stories derive enormous satisfaction from the gap between how the protagonist is initially perceived and what he eventually becomes capable of doing.

Shield Hero is messier and more divisive as it continues, and its revenge-oriented opening is stronger than some later stretches. But the first season in particular captures the progression fantasy that sends many viewers searching for 'anime like Solo Leveling' in the first place.
Watch this if:
your favorite part of
Solo Leveling
was seeing the weakest man in the room become someone nobody could dismiss again.
Which Anime Is Most Like Solo Leveling?
There is no perfect substitute because
Solo Leveling
combines several appeals that other anime usually separate.
For
leveling and boss mechanics
, start with
Shangri-La Frontier
. For
dungeons
, choose
DanMachi
. For
an absurdly powerful dark-clad protagonist
The Eminence in Shadow
is the obvious pick. For
Korean webtoon energy and a mysterious progression structure
, try
Tower of God
. For
modern supernatural fights
, go with
Jujutsu Kaisen
And if what you specifically loved was the transformation from 'weakest' to overwhelmingly capable,
The Rising of the Shield Hero
offers the most familiar emotional starting point even though its world and mechanics are very different.
What Makes Solo Leveling Hard to Replace?
Jinwoo's strength is not actually the unusual part. Anime has no shortage of protagonists who can overpower nearly everyone around them.
What
Solo Leveling
does unusually well is make
becoming overpowered
the spectacle.

Early Jinwoo is fragile enough that a low-level dungeon can kill him. The System then gives the audience a visible language for his transformation: quests, stats, classes, skills and increasingly difficult enemies. By the time other hunters begin treating him like an anomaly, viewers have watched the work that created that gap.

That is why recommendations based only on 'OP main character' often feel wrong. A character who begins unbeatable does not necessarily recreate the satisfaction of watching Jinwoo cross each threshold.

The Hunter world matters too. Ranks give strength a social meaning. Jinwoo is not merely stronger in Season 2 than he was in Season 1; he has moved through a hierarchy that once defined his entire identity. Our ranking of
every major S-Rank Hunter in Solo Leveling
shows just how far beyond that hierarchy his progression eventually takes him.
If You Want More Overpowered Protagonists
If this list still does not contain enough overwhelming main characters, the broader isekai genre is the obvious next rabbit hole.
Our updated ranking of the
10 best isekai anime to watch in 2026
includes
Re:Zero
Overlord
KonoSuba
Tensura
Mushoku Tensei
and other series that approach the 'another world' fantasy from very different directions.
Just remember that
Solo Leveling

itself is not really an isekai. Jinwoo does not reincarnate or permanently move into another world; the supernatural world invades his own through Gates and dungeons. The similarity is progression-fantasy structure, not genre classification.
The Best Place to Start After Solo Leveling
If you only want one recommendation, start with
Shangri-La Frontier
if the System-like progression and boss fights were your favorite part of
Solo Leveling
. Start with
The Eminence in Shadow
instead if you mainly want another protagonist who can enter a room and instantly make everyone else feel underleveled.
For something closer to
Solo Leveling
's Korean roots and mystery-driven world-building,
Tower of God
is the more interesting choice. And if you simply want another polished supernatural action series,
Jujutsu Kaisen
is the safest bet.
There is no anime that reproduces Jinwoo's journey exactly—and that is probably a good thing. The best follow-up is the one that identifies what you actually liked about
Solo Leveling
and gives you a different version of that feeling rather than a weaker copy.

faq.answer: Shangri-La Frontier is one of the closest choices if you like leveling, boss mechanics and visible progression. The Eminence in Shadow is better if you mainly want another overwhelmingly powerful, dark-clad protagonist, while Tower of God offers Korean-source fantasy built around climbing through a mysterious system.
faq.question: What anime is most similar to Solo Leveling?

faq.answer: Start with Shangri-La Frontier for progression and boss fights, The Eminence in Shadow for an overpowered protagonist, DanMachi for dungeon crawling, Tower of God for Korean webtoon fantasy, or Jujutsu Kaisen for high-end supernatural action.
faq.question: What should I watch after Solo Leveling?

faq.answer: No. Solo Leveling uses game-like mechanics and fantasy elements associated with isekai, but Sung Jinwoo remains in his own world. Gates and dungeons connect that world to supernatural spaces, so the series is better described as action fantasy and progression fantasy than traditional isekai.
faq.question: Is Solo Leveling an isekai anime?

faq.answer: Shangri-La Frontier and Sword Art Online have explicit game systems because their stories involve virtual worlds. DanMachi also provides visible adventurer growth and dungeon progression, although its mechanics work differently from Jinwoo's System.

children.text: Ghost in the Shell
has one of anime's strangest barriers to entry: people know it is important, but the franchise page looks like homework.
There is the 1995 movie. Then
Innocence
. Then
Stand Alone Complex
2nd GIG
and
Solid State Society
. Then
Arise
, which seems like a prequel until you realize it belongs to another continuity. Then
. And now there is
The Ghost in the Shell
, Science SARU's 2026 TV anime, which goes back to Masamune Shirow's manga rather than functioning as the next season of everything that came before.
The good news is that the watch order is much easier once you stop trying to force all of these anime into one timeline.
There is no single Ghost in the Shell anime continuity.

The franchise repeatedly reinterprets Motoko Kusanagi, Public Security Section 9 and Shirow's cyberpunk world. The best way to watch it is therefore to follow each continuity internally, while using the 1995 film as the ideal introduction to the franchise's central ideas.
Ghost in the Shell Watch Order — The Quick Answer
For a first-time viewer, this is the order I recommend:
Ghost in the Shell (1995)
Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence (2004)
Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex (2002)
Ghost in the Shell: S.A.C. 2nd GIG (2004)
Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex – Solid State Society (2006)
Ghost in the Shell: Arise – Border 1: Ghost Pain
Arise – Border 2: Ghost Whispers
Arise – Border 3: Ghost Tears
Arise – Border 4: Ghost Stands Alone
Arise – Alternative Architecture
Episodes 9–10 / the
Pyrophoric Cult
material
Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie (2015)
Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045 Season 1
Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045 Season 2
The Ghost in the Shell (2026)
That is a
franchise tour
, not one chronological storyline. The most important rule is simpler: never jump from one continuity to another expecting the previous story to continue.
The Four Main Ghost in the Shell Anime Continuities
The cleanest way to understand the franchise is to divide it into four interpretations.
1. Mamoru Oshii's Film Continuity
Ghost in the Shell
Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence
These films are the philosophical, atmospheric version that made
Ghost in the Shell
an international cyberpunk landmark.
2. Stand Alone Complex Continuity
Stand Alone Complex
S.A.C. 2nd GIG
Solid State Society
Seasons 1 and 2
This is the longest anime continuity and the best choice if you want to spend substantial time with Section 9 as a team.
3. Arise Continuity
Arise
Borders 1–4
Pyrophoric Cult
/ the additional
Alternative Architecture
material
Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie
This continuity reimagines a younger Motoko and the formation of the Section 9 team.
4. The Ghost in the Shell (2026)
Science SARU's new television series is another adaptation of Masamune Shirow's manga, not
SAC_2045 Season 3
. Shirow himself described the 2026 production as a new version following the anime interpretations associated with Mamoru Oshii, Kenji Kamiyama and Kazuchika Kise.
We have a separate analysis of
why The Ghost in the Shell 2026 returns to Masamune Shirow's original cyberpunk vision
, which is worth reading once you understand where the new series sits.
1. Start With Ghost in the Shell (1995)
If you have never seen anything from the franchise, start here.

Mamoru Oshii's 1995 film follows Major Motoko Kusanagi and Section 9 as they pursue the Puppet Master, an entity capable of infiltrating cyberized minds. The investigation gradually becomes something much stranger than a police case, forcing Motoko to question where consciousness begins and whether an artificial intelligence can possess a self.
The movie is compact, visually extraordinary and foundational. It teaches you the vocabulary of the franchise—
ghosts, shells, cyberbrains, Section 9, Motoko, Batou
—without requiring knowledge of any other adaptation.
More importantly, it establishes the question that almost every later version keeps rewriting: when memories, bodies and information can all be manipulated, what remains of a person?
The 1995 movie is not a pilot for
Stand Alone Complex
. Watch it as its own interpretation.
2. Watch Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence Next
Innocence
is the direct follow-up to Oshii's film and should be watched after the 1995 movie.

The focus shifts heavily toward Batou as Section 9 investigates murders involving gynoids—androids created to resemble women. Motoko's presence is different after the events of the first film, and the sequel assumes you understand what happened to her.
Innocence

is denser and more deliberately alienating than its predecessor. Characters quote philosophy and literature while the movie lingers on artificial bodies, ritual, animals and the increasingly unstable boundary between human and machine.
If the first movie made you curious about
Ghost in the Shell
as philosophy,
Innocence
pushes much harder in that direction.
3. Then Start Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex
After the films, reset your expectations.
Stand Alone Complex
is a
different continuity
. Motoko is back leading Section 9, familiar characters return in different circumstances, and the Puppet Master storyline from the 1995 film is not the history you are continuing from.
That freedom allows the television series to build a much larger world.

The first season combines self-contained cybercrime investigations with the Laughing Man case, a conspiracy involving corporations, government institutions, hacking and information control. The title's idea of a 'Stand Alone Complex' becomes part of the show's larger interest in how behavior and narratives can spread even without a single original author directing them.

For viewers who find the 1995 movie fascinating but emotionally distant, SAC is often where the franchise truly clicks. Togusa, Batou, Aramaki and the rest of Section 9 have more room to become people rather than functions inside a two-hour story.
4. Continue With S.A.C. 2nd GIG
Do not skip directly to
Solid State Society
2nd GIG
is the second television season of
Stand Alone Complex

and develops the same version of Section 9. Its central conflict revolves around refugees, political instability and the Individual Eleven, while the series continues mixing major serialized developments with smaller investigations.
If Season 1 shows how information can generate a social phenomenon,
2nd GIG
becomes more explicitly political. Borders, nationalism, displacement, terrorism and state power all become part of the cyberpunk machinery.
The two SAC seasons are best treated as one long piece of television rather than separate reboots.
5. Watch Solid State Society After 2nd GIG
Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex – Solid State Society
takes place after
2nd GIG
and functions as the next major chapter in the SAC continuity.

The official Ghost in the Shell site places the story in 2034, two years after the Refugee Uprising Incident. Section 9 has expanded, Motoko's relationship with the organization has changed, and a new case points toward a hacker known as the Puppeteer.
The movie works because it assumes you have spent 52 television episodes learning how this version of Section 9 operates. Watching it too early removes much of that weight.
So for SAC, the rule is straightforward:
Season 1 → 2nd GIG → Solid State Society.
Where Do The Laughing Man and Individual Eleven Movies Fit?
You may encounter titles called
The Laughing Man
and
Individual Eleven
while searching the franchise.
These are compilation versions of the major storylines from the first two
Stand Alone Complex
seasons. They are not required sequels.

For a first watch, I strongly recommend the full TV seasons. The standalone investigations are not meaningless filler; they establish the world, the team and the thematic texture that makes the larger cases more effective.
Use the compilation movies for a refresher or a shorter rewatch, not as the ideal replacement for your first experience.
6. Start Arise as a Separate Universe

body.alt: Ghost in the Shell Arise promotional artwork featuring Motoko Kusanagi and the Section 9 team
body.insertAfterHeading: ## 6. Start Arise as a Separate Universe

children.text: Once you finish the classic films and SAC material—or whenever you want another interpretation—you can begin
Ghost in the Shell: Arise
Arise

reimagines Motoko at an earlier stage of her career and builds toward the formation of the familiar Section 9 team. The character designs, voices and continuity are different because this is not a hidden prequel to Oshii's movie or
Stand Alone Complex
Watch the original Borders in numerical order:
Border 1: Ghost Pain
Border 2: Ghost Whispers
Border 3: Ghost Tears
Border 4: Ghost Stands Alone
That is the cleanest way to experience the core
Arise
story.
What Is Arise: Alternative Architecture?
This is where the franchise makes a simple order look unnecessarily complicated.
Ghost in the Shell: Arise – Alternative Architecture
repackages the
Arise
material for television. Most of it overlaps with the four Borders, so you do
not
need to watch the same story twice.
The important exception is the additional
Pyrophoric Cult
storyline, represented by the new episodes added to the television version. That material bridges the core
Arise
story toward
The New Movie
So the efficient order is: watch Borders 1–4, then watch the
new Pyrophoric Cult material
, then continue to
The New Movie
If the service you use only offers
Alternative Architecture
, you can watch that version instead of hunting down every original Border. Just remember that it is another presentation of substantially overlapping material, not a sequel to all four OVAs.
7. Finish the Arise Timeline With The New Movie
Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie
from 2015 belongs to the
Arise
continuity despite its generic-sounding title.

This is the payoff to that version's younger Motoko and its gradual construction of Section 9. Watching it immediately after the 1995 film because both are called movies would be a mistake; they are different interpretations with different histories.
Once you treat
Arise
as its own lane, the order becomes easy:
Arise → Pyrophoric Cult → The New Movie.
8. Where Does SAC_2045 Fit?
belongs to the
Stand Alone Complex continuity
That means the ideal background is:
Stand Alone Complex → 2nd GIG → Solid State Society → SAC_2045 Season 1 → SAC_2045 Season 2.

The visual change is enormous. SAC_2045 uses 3DCG animation, and its aesthetic is very different from the earlier Production I.G television series. But continuity-wise, it is much closer to SAC than its appearance might suggest.

The story moves Section 9 into a world shaped by economic collapse, 'Sustainable War' and the emergence of Posthumans. If you watch it without the earlier SAC material, you can understand much of the immediate plot, but the returning relationships carry considerably more meaning when you know this version of the team.
What About the SAC_2045 Compilation Movies?
As with the older SAC compilation films, you may find movie versions of the SAC_2045 material.
They are condensed presentations rather than an essential separate continuation. If you are watching the two full seasons, you do not need the compilation movies to understand the story.
That principle saves a lot of time across this franchise:
do not mistake recap or compilation editions for mandatory new entries.
9. Where Does The Ghost in the Shell 2026 Fit?
This is the biggest update to the watch order in 2026.
Science SARU's
The Ghost in the Shell
began airing in July 2026. It is based on Masamune Shirow's original manga and represents another anime interpretation rather than a continuation of

The production is directed by Mokochan, with series composition and scripts by EnJoe Toh, character design and chief animation direction by Shuhei Handa, and animation production by Science SARU. The official franchise site lists it alongside the Oshii films, SAC, Arise and SAC_2045 as its own major branch.
That means
you can watch the 2026 series without finishing every older Ghost in the Shell anime first

In fact, viewers who have only seen the 1995 film can comfortably approach it as a new adaptation. The contrast is fascinating: Oshii's film distills Shirow's material into something solemn and meditative, while the 2026 anime has more room to reconnect with the manga's energy, humor and version of Motoko.
Our article on
The Ghost in the Shell 2026 and Masamune Shirow's original vision
goes deeper into precisely that difference.
Can I Start With the 2026 Ghost in the Shell Anime?
Yes.
If your interest in the franchise comes specifically from Science SARU's new series, you do not need to watch decades of anime first. It is not Season 3 of SAC_2045 or a sequel to
Innocence
Still, I would watch the
1995 film
at some point. Not because the 2026 series requires it, but because seeing how two very different creative teams interpret the same source ideas is one of the pleasures of
Ghost in the Shell
The new anime is currently streaming globally on Prime Video, which makes it one of the easiest modern entry points into the franchise.
Should You Watch Ghost in the Shell in Release Order?
Release order works surprisingly well if your goal is to understand how the franchise evolved as anime.
You begin with Oshii's film interpretation, move into the expansive television approach of
Stand Alone Complex
, see
Arise
reconstruct Motoko's origins, watch SAC return through
, and finally reach Science SARU's manga-focused 2026 reinterpretation.
The disadvantage is that release order makes you bounce between continuities. A newcomer can easily assume that familiar characters mean the same timeline is continuing.
That is why I prefer a
continuity-first release order
: start with the 1995 films, watch SAC internally in order, then Arise internally in order, then SAC_2045, and approach the 2026 anime as its own adaptation.
Is There a Chronological Ghost in the Shell Watch Order?
Not for the franchise as a whole.
You can create chronological orders
inside individual continuities
, but there is no meaningful master chronology in which
Arise
simply happens before the 1995 movie and SAC happens afterward.
Those stories contradict and reinterpret one another because they were never designed as chapters of one history.
This is the most important thing a watch-order guide can tell you. Trying to solve
Ghost in the Shell
like a single Marvel-style timeline creates confusion that the franchise itself does not require.
The Best Stand Alone Complex Watch Order
If you only care about SAC, use this order:
Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex
Ghost in the Shell: S.A.C. 2nd GIG
Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex – Solid State Society
Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045 Season 1
Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045 Season 2
Skip the compilation movies on your first run.
This is also the version I would recommend to someone who wants
cybercrime investigations, political conspiracies and a larger Section 9 ensemble
rather than the more concentrated philosophical atmosphere of Oshii's films.
The Best Arise Watch Order
For
Arise
, use:
Border 1: Ghost Pain
Border 2: Ghost Whispers
Border 3: Ghost Tears
Border 4: Ghost Stands Alone
Pyrophoric Cult
/ the new
Alternative Architecture
episodes
Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie
Do not watch all four Borders and then the entirety of
Alternative Architecture
unless you deliberately want to revisit the same material in its TV edit.
What About Ghost in the Shell 2.0?
Ghost in the Shell 2.0
is a revised version of the 1995 film, not a sequel.
It updates parts of the movie with new digital effects and altered presentation. For a first viewing, I recommend the
original 1995 version
. It is the historically important version and preserves the visual texture that made the film so influential.
Watch 2.0 later if you are curious about the differences.
Does the 2017 Live-Action Ghost in the Shell Movie Matter?
No—not for an anime watch order.
The 2017 Hollywood film starring Scarlett Johansson is another adaptation drawing from ideas and imagery associated with the franchise, but it is not required to understand any anime continuity.
You can watch it as a curiosity after becoming familiar with the franchise, but leaving it out does not create a gap in the anime story.
Which Ghost in the Shell Should You Watch First?
For most people:
Ghost in the Shell (1995).
It is short enough to sample the franchise in one sitting and influential enough that even viewers who decide not to continue will understand why the name matters.
But there are two reasonable alternatives.
Start with
Stand Alone Complex
if you strongly prefer television, procedural investigations and ensemble casts. Start with
The Ghost in the Shell (2026)
if the new Science SARU adaptation is specifically what brought you here.
There is no continuity penalty for doing either.
If cerebral science fiction is your main interest, AnimeSparks' piece on
why Steins;Gate is one of the best sci-fi anime ever made
is also a natural next read. For something colder and more opaque, our
Ergo Proxy explanation
covers another anime preoccupied with identity, artificial life and what remains human in a technologically transformed world.
Do You Need to Watch Everything?
Absolutely not.
This is the other mistake watch-order guides can encourage.
Ghost in the Shell
is not a franchise where skipping one 2000s television episode prevents you from understanding a reboot made twenty years later.
If you only want the essentials, watch:
Ghost in the Shell (1995) → Stand Alone Complex → 2nd GIG → The Ghost in the Shell (2026).
Add
Innocence
if you love Oshii's approach. Add
Solid State Society
and SAC_2045 if SAC becomes your favorite continuity. Add
Arise
if you want a different take on how Motoko and Section 9 come together.
That modular structure is a strength, not a flaw.
The Best Ghost in the Shell Watch Order for Newcomers
My recommendation is to think in
versions of Ghost in the Shell
, not dates inside one fictional universe.
Start with the 1995 movie because it remains the cleanest introduction to Motoko Kusanagi and the franchise's central questions. Continue to
Innocence
while that film's continuity is fresh. Then reset and give
Stand Alone Complex
room to build its own version of Section 9. Follow SAC through
2nd GIG
and
Solid State Society
, and save
for when you want to return to that continuity later.
Treat
Arise
as another beginning. Treat the 2026 Science SARU anime as another beginning too.
Once you understand that,
Ghost in the Shell
stops looking like a tangled chronology and starts looking like what it really is:
several generations of anime creators arguing with the same extraordinary set of ideas about consciousness, technology, identity and the future of the human body.

children.text: Disney and Square Enix are finally taking
Kingdom Hearts
somewhere fans have imagined for years: television. An original animated series inspired by the games was announced during D23 2026, with Disney confirming that it is being developed for
Disney Channel and Disney+
in partnership with
Kingdom Hearts
creator Tetsuya Nomura and the creative team at Square Enix.
The most important detail is also the most intriguing. This is not being presented as a simple scene-for-scene retelling of the first game. Disney says the series will
reimagine the iconic adventure with a brand-new story that expands the Kingdom Hearts universe
. That makes the project potentially relevant not only to newcomers, but to fans who have spent years following Sora, Riku, Kairi, the Keyblade and the franchise's increasingly complicated mythology.
When Is the Kingdom Hearts Anime Coming Out?
There is
no exact Kingdom Hearts anime release date yet

Disney's announcement says the series is "coming soon," but as of August 2026 it has not announced a premiere day, month or year. Reports following the D23 reveal also note that an episode count, animation studio and voice cast remain unannounced.

That distinction matters. With a project this early in its public rollout, any specific release window circulating without a Disney or Square Enix announcement should be treated as speculation rather than confirmation.
What
is
confirmed is that the series has been greenlit and is intended for both Disney Channel and Disney+.
For readers following other major adaptations without firm dates, our
Kagurabachi anime release date guide
uses the same confirmed-versus-unconfirmed approach as announcements develop.
What Exactly Did Disney Announce?
Disney revealed the animated
Kingdom Hearts
project around D23 2026, where the franchise was celebrating its 25th anniversary. The company had already scheduled a dedicated
DEEP DIVE into KINGDOM HEARTS
presentation as part of the event's programming.
The new show is described as an
original Kingdom Hearts anime series inspired by the video game franchise
. Disney's announcement places it on Disney Channel and Disney+, while coverage of the reveal states that the project is being developed with Tetsuya Nomura and Square Enix's creative team.
That collaboration is arguably the biggest reason longtime fans should pay attention.
Tetsuya Nomura's Involvement Matters
Tetsuya Nomura has guided
Kingdom Hearts

since the franchise began in 2002. Square Enix itself describes the series as led by Nomura, and his influence is inseparable from its characters, visual identity and enormous interconnected mythology.
Having Nomura and Square Enix involved gives the animated series a much closer connection to the creative source than a loosely licensed adaptation would have.
It does
not

, however, automatically tell us where the anime sits in canon. Disney has not yet publicly laid out a precise chronological placement. Until it does, theories connecting the show directly to a particular game, cancelled project or unseen period in the timeline should remain theories.
That kind of continuity question is familiar to anime fans. Our
Ghost in the Shell watch order
shows how dramatically different continuities can change the best way to approach a franchise.
Kingdom Hearts
may eventually need similar clarity once we know exactly what this series is doing.
Will the Kingdom Hearts Anime Retell the Games?
Not in the straightforward way many people initially expected.
The official description says the series will
reimagine the iconic adventure with a brand-new story

while expanding the universe and celebrating characters fans already know. That wording leaves room for familiar events, worlds and relationships, but it strongly suggests the show has ambitions beyond merely animating the original 2002 game's cutscenes.
That is probably the more interesting choice.
A direct adaptation would immediately face a structural problem:
Kingdom Hearts
is no longer one clean story told across three numbered games. Its mythology stretches through
Chain of Memories
358/2 Days
Birth by Sleep
Dream Drop Distance
Kingdom Hearts III
, mobile-era lore and other entries whose events often become essential later.

An original story can potentially introduce the emotional foundations—friendship, separation, memory, hearts, light and darkness—without forcing a television audience to digest every branch of the game chronology at once.
What Could the Story Be About?
For now, this is where confirmed information ends and interpretation begins.

Disney has not released a detailed synopsis. The promotional material has deliberately given fans very little to work with, and the mysterious Keyblade-bearing figure in the early imagery has already generated theories.
The safest expectation is that the series will preserve the central language of
Kingdom Hearts
: worlds connected across a larger cosmology, Keyblades, the conflict between light and darkness, and characters whose bonds survive separation and loss.
Whether Sora is the sole protagonist, shares the focus with another character or is used as an entry point into a new corner of the universe remains unconfirmed.
That uncertainty may actually be intentional.
Kingdom Hearts
has always turned unanswered questions into part of the experience.
Will Sora, Donald and Goofy Be in the Anime?

body.alt: Official Kingdom Hearts III promotional artwork featuring Sora, Donald Duck and Goofy
body.insertAfterHeading: Will Sora, Donald and Goofy Be in the Anime?

children.text: Disney has said the series will celebrate characters associated with the franchise, but a full character roster has not been announced.

Sora is naturally the character most viewers will expect. He is the Keyblade-wielding hero at the center of the main games, while Donald Duck and Goofy form the trio that travels through Disney and Pixar worlds with him. Riku and Kairi are equally fundamental to Sora's personal story.
Still, there is an important difference between
likely
and
officially cast
. Until Disney reveals character sheets, footage or a voice cast, we should not treat every familiar face as confirmed for a major role.
Where Will the Kingdom Hearts Anime Stream?
Disney has confirmed
Disney+
as a home for the series, alongside
Disney Channel
Regional availability and whether episodes will launch simultaneously worldwide have not been detailed. Those distribution specifics will likely become clearer closer to release.

For anime viewers used to tracking platform announcements, this is a different situation from titles built primarily around anime streaming services. Disney is directly involved in the franchise itself, making Disney+ a natural destination rather than merely an overseas licensing partner.
Our
best anime on Netflix guide
looks at how streaming platforms have increasingly become major entry points into anime;
Kingdom Hearts
could expose another enormous audience to Japanese-led franchise storytelling through Disney's own ecosystem.
Which Studio Is Animating Kingdom Hearts?
The animation studio has
not been officially announced

That is one of the biggest outstanding questions. "Anime" describes the project in Disney's announcement, but fans should not assume a particular Japanese studio is attached until Disney or Square Enix names one.

The eventual studio reveal will tell us much more about the project's visual ambitions: whether it aims to closely reproduce Nomura's game designs, reinterpret them for television, or build a distinct visual identity around the new story.
Has the Voice Cast Been Announced?
No full voice cast has been announced as of August 2026.

That means it is too early to state whether performers associated with the games will reprise their roles across the series. Returning voices would create immediate continuity for longtime players, but Disney has not yet confirmed its casting strategy.
Do You Need to Play the Games Before Watching?
Probably not if Disney truly intends this as a reimagined adventure, although longtime players are likely to recognize far more of its mythology.

A television adaptation needs an accessible doorway. If viewers had to finish a long list of games before episode one, the series would struggle to function as its own show. The promise of a brand-new story gives the creators a chance to introduce concepts organically rather than expecting newcomers to arrive with a timeline diagram.
At the same time,
Kingdom Hearts
is built on accumulated emotional history. Existing fans will inevitably examine every symbol, Keyblade and seemingly casual line for connections to the games.
That balance—accessible on the surface, deeper for established fans—is what could make the adaptation work.
Anime viewers who enjoy sprawling fantasy worlds can also see our
10 best isekai anime to watch in 2026
Kingdom Hearts
is not conventional isekai, but its world-hopping structure scratches a similar itch for discovery and radically different settings.
Why Kingdom Hearts Makes Sense as an Anime

body.alt: Kingdom Hearts promotional artwork featuring Sora, Riku, Kairi and other major characters beneath a heart-shaped moon
body.insertAfterHeading: Why Kingdom Hearts Makes Sense as an Anime

children.text: The surprise is not that
Kingdom Hearts
can become animation. The surprise is that it took this long for a full series to happen.

The franchise already thinks like animation. Its storytelling moves between expressive character drama, surreal metaphysics, large-scale action and Disney worlds with completely different visual identities. Sora can stand beside Donald and Goofy in one sequence and confront an original Square Enix-style antagonist in another without the tonal collision feeling accidental. That collision is the premise.
Animation also frees the adaptation from trying to make the Keyblade, Heartless and Disney characters coexist convincingly in live action. It can embrace exaggeration rather than apologize for it.
The challenge is narrative clarity. The games are beloved partly because their mythology is so elaborate, but television needs momentum. A successful anime has to preserve the strange sincerity of
Kingdom Hearts
without turning every episode into an explanation of terminology.
The Biggest Questions Still Unanswered
Several important details remain open after the announcement:
What is the exact release date?
Which animation studio is producing the series?
Who is directing it?
Who are the main characters?
Which voice actors will return or join the franchise?
How does the new story relate to the games' canon?
Which Disney and Pixar worlds will appear?
How many episodes will the first season have?
Will Disney+ release it weekly or all at once?
Those are not minor details, but the announcement is still significant because the hardest step has already happened:
Kingdom Hearts is officially becoming a television series
Why This Could Become One of Disney+'s Most Interesting Animated Projects
Kingdom Hearts

occupies an unusual space. It is simultaneously a Disney crossover, a Square Enix action RPG, a Japanese fantasy saga and a decades-long serialized mystery. A television series has access to all of those identities, but it will succeed only if it understands why they work together.
The involvement of Nomura and Square Enix makes the new-story approach much more interesting than a generic adaptation. It creates the possibility that the anime can feel like an actual addition to
Kingdom Hearts
, rather than a simplified recap created outside the franchise's creative orbit.
For now, the correct answer to
when does the Kingdom Hearts anime come out?
is simple: Disney has confirmed the series for Disney Channel and Disney+, but
an exact release date has not yet been announced
We will know much more once Disney reveals the studio, cast, first trailer and premiere window. Until then, the mystery surrounding the series feels strangely appropriate for
Kingdom Hearts

children.text: Haikyu!!
is finally ready to continue the Spring High after
The Dumpster Battle
, and this time the anime is tackling
two quarterfinal matches happening at the same stage of the tournament
There is one important clarification, though: despite the two projects sometimes being described together as the next two
Haikyu!!
releases,
they are not officially two movies
. The first is a theatrical film,
Haikyu!! VS The Little Giant
. The second,
Haikyu!! Where the Monsters Go
Bakemono-tachi no Iku Tokoro
), is officially described as a
special anime
. Both are scheduled for 2027.

That distinction actually makes the plan more interesting. Rather than forcing every remaining Spring High storyline into one film, Production I.G is giving Karasuno's next match the theatrical spotlight while also adapting the huge Fukurodani vs. Mujinazaka showdown separately.
When Are the New Haikyu!! Anime Projects Coming Out?
Both
Haikyu!! VS The Little Giant
and
Haikyu!! Where the Monsters Go
are officially scheduled for
As of August 2026, the official
Haikyu!!
site has not announced an exact premiere date for either project.
VS The Little Giant
is confirmed for theatrical release in Japan, while the official site now says
Where the Monsters Go
will air in 2027.
So the confirmed status is simple:
two new Haikyu!! anime projects in 2027, but only one of them is currently billed as a movie.
That is worth keeping clear because search results and fan discussion can easily turn "two new anime projects" into "two new movies."
The First Project: Haikyu!! VS The Little Giant

body.insertAfterHeading: ## The First Project: Haikyu!! VS The Little Giant

children.text: The headline event is
Haikyu!! VS The Little Giant
, the theatrical continuation of Karasuno's Spring High run.
After surviving the extraordinary match against Nekoma in
The Dumpster Battle
, Karasuno advances to the quarterfinals. Waiting for Hinata and the team is
Kamomedai High
, led by Korai Hoshiumi.
Hoshiumi is not just another elite opponent. He is one of the most important players Hinata could possibly meet at this point in his story.

Both are undersized attackers competing in a sport that constantly rewards height. Both can jump at an exceptional level. Both refuse to accept that being short should define the ceiling of what they can become. But Hoshiumi is not simply "another Hinata." He represents a more complete version of the path Hinata has been chasing.
That is why the title
VS The Little Giant
matters.
Hinata began
Haikyu!!

inspired by Karasuno's legendary Little Giant. Now he faces a player carrying the same kind of reputation—and the match forces him to reconsider what becoming a great volleyball player actually means.
Our existing essay on
why Haikyu!! is about effort without a promise of greatness
is particularly relevant here, because Hinata vs. Hoshiumi pushes that idea harder than almost any previous match.
Hinata vs. Hoshiumi Is More Than a Rivalry
It would be easy to market the movie as a simple battle between two short, explosive players. The manga gives the matchup much more weight than that.

Hinata has spent much of the series trying to compensate for what he lacks. His speed, jumping ability and partnership with Kageyama allow him to break through defenses that should overwhelm him physically. But his journey has also been about realizing that spectacular athleticism alone is not enough.
Hoshiumi is dangerous because his game is broader. He forces Hinata to look at skills beyond the one thing that originally made him feel special.

The movie therefore arrives at exactly the right point in Hinata's development. After the emotional fulfillment of finally playing Nekoma on the national stage, Karasuno immediately faces a match that asks a much less nostalgic question:
how much further does Hinata still have to go?
Who Is Kamomedai High?
Kamomedai is built to make Karasuno uncomfortable.

Hoshiumi may be the obvious star, but reducing the team to him would miss why this quarterfinal is so difficult. Kamomedai is disciplined, technically formidable and especially dangerous at the net. Their blocking creates a different problem from the chaotic familiarity Karasuno experienced against Nekoma.
That matters for the movie's structure.
The Dumpster Battle
could draw on years of history between Karasuno and Nekoma.
VS The Little Giant

has to generate its tension differently: through the volleyball itself, through Hinata's confrontation with Hoshiumi, and through the feeling that Karasuno has reached a stage where every opponent can end their tournament.
The Second Project: Haikyu!! Where the Monsters Go

children.text: While Karasuno faces Kamomedai, another Spring High quarterfinal is happening elsewhere.
Fukurodani Academy vs. Mujinazaka High
will be adapted in the special anime
Haikyu!! Where the Monsters Go
For fans of Kotaro Bokuto, this is a major piece of the remaining story.
Bokuto has always been one of
Haikyu!!

's most charismatic players: loud, emotional, explosive and capable of turning a match into his personal stage. But his larger arc is not about becoming less emotional. It is about becoming a player who can carry his team without requiring everyone around him to constantly carry his mood.
Mujinazaka gives that growth the perfect opponent.
Bokuto vs. Kiryu Is the Match Fans Have Been Waiting For
Mujinazaka is led by
Wakatsu Kiryu
, one of Japan's nationally recognized top high-school aces.

That immediately gives Bokuto a measuring stick beyond personality and popularity. This is a match involving two elite aces with very different relationships to pressure, responsibility and their own strength.
The official site's newest action preview emphasizes exactly that confrontation, showing Bokuto and Kiryu trading powerful spikes while both teams collide at full intensity.
For Bokuto, this is one of the matches that shows why Fukurodani is not merely a colorful rival school orbiting Karasuno. They have their own national tournament to win.
That is why adapting the match separately is such a good decision. Compressing it into a few scenes inside Karasuno's movie would turn an important character payoff into background information.
Why Are These Two Matches Being Released Separately?
The two quarterfinals occur during the same phase of the Spring High tournament, but they serve very different characters.
VS The Little Giant
belongs primarily to
Hinata, Hoshiumi and Karasuno's attempt to keep advancing
Where the Monsters Go
gives
Bokuto, Kiryu, Fukurodani and Mujinazaka
the space their match needs.

This also addresses one of the biggest concerns fans had after the anime moved from television seasons to theatrical releases: there is a lot of manga material left, and volleyball matches lose their impact when too many rallies and character beats are compressed.
A dedicated special does not guarantee that every manga scene will survive, but it gives the Fukurodani match far more room than treating it as a side plot inside the movie.
Is Where the Monsters Go a Movie?
Officially,
no
The Japanese
Haikyu!!
site consistently labels
VS The Little Giant
as a theatrical film and
Where the Monsters Go
as a
special anime
. The latest August 2026 update says the special anime will be broadcast in 2027.

That does not make it a minor project. It is adapting one of the major Spring High quarterfinals and has received its own promotional visuals and footage. But readers looking for "the two new Haikyu movies" should know the precise format.
What Happened Before These New Projects?
The last major anime installment was
Haikyu!! The Dumpster Battle
, released in Japan in 2024.
That film finally delivered Karasuno vs. Nekoma on the national stage—the match the series had been building toward since the teams first began practicing against each other. The official
Haikyu!!
site reports that the film surpassed
20 billion yen in worldwide box office revenue
, underlining how successfully the franchise transitioned from television into theaters.
VS The Little Giant
begins from the aftermath of that victory. Karasuno does not get a long emotional break. The Spring High bracket keeps moving.
That is important for newcomers returning after a gap:
watch The Dumpster Battle before the 2027 movie.
Who Is Making Haikyu!! VS The Little Giant?
Production I.G
is returning for animation production, maintaining the studio connection that has defined the anime since the television series began.
The official movie site also lists
Susumu Mitsunaka
as director and scriptwriter. Mitsunaka directed the earlier
Haikyu!!
television seasons and returned to direct
The Dumpster Battle
, so the new film continues with a filmmaker deeply familiar with the series' visual language.
That continuity matters in a sports anime where camera placement, rhythm and the sensation of impact are part of the storytelling.
Haikyu!!
has always worked because the animation does more than show where the ball goes—it communicates what a rally feels like to the player trying desperately to reach it.
Will the Original Voice Cast Return?

The familiar anime cast is expected around the returning characters shown in the projects, but readers should distinguish promotional appearances from a complete formal cast announcement for every role.
As more 2027 release information arrives, the official site should provide fuller cast and staff listings. The most important new matchup characters are already central to the promotional campaign:
Shoyo Hinata and Korai Hoshiumi
for the movie, and
Kotaro Bokuto and Wakatsu Kiryu
for the special anime.
How Much of the Manga Will the Movie Cover?
The movie is centered on
Karasuno vs. Kamomedai
, while the special anime handles
Fukurodani vs. Mujinazaka
Beyond those confirmed matchups, it is better not to pretend we know the exact adaptation boundaries until the final runtime and additional story details are announced.

That is especially important because the remaining manga contains material after these quarterfinals that is essential to the ending of Hinata's story. The existence of these two projects answers what happens next immediately after Nekoma; it does
not yet answer exactly how Production I.G plans to animate every remaining chapter of the manga
Fans should therefore be cautious with claims that these releases alone will necessarily complete the entire anime.
Will There Be Another Haikyu!! Movie After VS The Little Giant?
No additional movie after
VS The Little Giant
has been officially announced as of August 2026.
The franchise previously announced a "FINAL" theatrical project, which naturally led to expectations about how the remaining manga would be divided. The addition of
Where the Monsters Go
demonstrates that the production can use formats outside the main theatrical films to adapt important material.
That makes the ultimate shape of the anime ending more interesting—but also less certain.
Until the production committee announces the next project, the safest answer is that
VS The Little Giant and Where the Monsters Go are the two confirmed upcoming anime releases
Why 2027 Could Be Huge for Haikyu!!
The next phase has something
The Dumpster Battle
did not: two different visions of what a top-level ace can look like.
Hinata confronts Hoshiumi, another short player who refuses to be limited by height. Bokuto confronts Kiryu, another nationally elite ace carrying a very different psychological burden.
Those matches echo each other without being the same story. One asks Hinata to reconsider the identity he has chased since childhood. The other asks Bokuto to prove what kind of ace he has become.
And both happen under the pressure of a national tournament where there is no reset button. A loss does not create a training arc. It ends the run.
That is where
Haikyu!!

has always been strongest. The series loves improvement, but it never promises that effort will be rewarded with the exact victory a character wants. That tension is why its matches can remain suspenseful even after hundreds of chapters of growth.
What We Still Don't Know
Several major details remain unconfirmed:
The exact 2027 release date for
VS The Little Giant
The exact 2027 broadcast date for
Where the Monsters Go
The movie's final runtime
International theatrical dates
Global streaming plans for the special anime
Complete cast and staff details for both projects
Exactly how the anime will adapt the manga material that follows these quarterfinals
Those unknowns should become clearer as the 2027 promotional campaign accelerates.
What Should You Watch Before the New Haikyu!! Movie?
If you are already caught up through Season 4, the essential next step is
Haikyu!! The Dumpster Battle
. The new movie directly follows Karasuno's match against Nekoma at Spring High.
You do not need a complicated watch order beyond that. The emotional context for Hoshiumi, Bokuto and the national tournament has been built across the TV anime, while
The Dumpster Battle
brings Karasuno to the exact point where these two new projects begin.
For readers returning to the franchise after several years away, our
Haikyu!! essay on effort, failure and greatness
is a useful reminder of why the series' philosophy matters so much heading into the quarterfinals.
The Real Reason These Two Projects Matter
It is tempting to reduce the 2027 announcements to bigger matches and bigger animation. But this stretch of
Haikyu!!
is important because the characters are running out of time.

High-school sports stories have a built-in ending that battle anime do not. Tournaments finish. Third-years graduate. Teams change. The match a player has spent years preparing for can end in an afternoon.
VS The Little Giant
and
Where the Monsters Go
arrive at the point where that reality becomes impossible to ignore.
Karasuno has finally defeated Nekoma. Fukurodani has reached the national quarterfinals. Hinata and Bokuto look more capable than ever. And none of that guarantees what happens in the next match.
That is why 2027 is shaping up to be one of the most important years the
Haikyu!!
anime has had. One movie will put Hinata face-to-face with a different Little Giant. One special will finally give Bokuto's national-stage battle the focus it deserves.
For now, the release information is straightforward:
Haikyu!! VS The Little Giant will open in Japanese theaters in 2027, and Haikyu!! Where the Monsters Go will also air in 2027. Exact dates have not yet been announced.
