children.text: Dandadan Season 3 is officially scheduled to air in 2027, with Science SARU continuing as the animation studio. An exact month and premiere date have not been announced, so any claim that the season is locked to a specific 2027 anime cour is still speculation.
Dandadan Season 3 release window

The official anime team has confirmed only the year: 2027. That means there is currently no verified January, April, July or October premiere window. The distinction matters because production announcements often arrive long before broadcasters finalize a particular television season, and a teaser visual is not the same thing as a dated broadcast notice.
Science SARU is returning

Science SARU is confirmed to continue producing the anime. That gives Season 3 creative continuity with the previous adaptation, whose appeal depends heavily on the studio's ability to move between frantic action, horror imagery, absurd comedy and surprisingly sincere character moments. Dandadan changes tone quickly, so keeping the same studio is more meaningful here than a simple production-credit detail.
What the Season 3 teaser tells us

The Season 3 teaser visual places Momo, Okarun and Turbo Granny around a mysterious girl emerging from what looks like a space-monster suit. That is useful story direction without being a full synopsis. It signals that the anime will continue escalating the extraterrestrial side of Dandadan's world while keeping its core cast at the center.

Anime-only viewers do not need to know manga arc names to understand the setup. Dandadan repeatedly takes unfinished consequences from one supernatural encounter and turns them into the trigger for the next. Season 3 is expected to continue directly from the material already animated rather than beginning a separate story.
What to expect from Momo and Okarun

The paranormal battles are only half of Dandadan. The series keeps returning to Momo and Okarun's awkward relationship, jealousy, loyalty and inability to say what they actually mean. A useful Season 3 preview should therefore not reduce the new season to a list of monsters. The emotional progression between the two leads is likely to remain as important as whatever new alien or occult threat appears next.
Will the cast return?

The returning production strongly suggests continuity for the established characters, but a complete Season 3 cast list should only be treated as final once the official site publishes it for the new season. New characters shown in promotional art can also lead to additional voice-cast announcements closer to broadcast.
Where will Dandadan Season 3 stream?

The Dandadan franchise has broad international streaming partners in different territories. That does not guarantee identical Season 3 availability everywhere. Until the 2027 simulcast lineups are published, the safest statement is that the season is confirmed for 2027 while regional streaming schedules remain to be announced.
What remains unannounced

There is still no exact premiere date, episode count, confirmed cour, complete staff list or global release timetable. Those gaps are normal this far from broadcast. The most useful way to follow Season 3 is to separate the official 2027 confirmation and Science SARU's return from predictions about when in 2027 the anime will actually begin.

AnimeSparks will update this guide when the production announces a month, dated trailer, additional cast, theme songs or streaming details. Until then, 2027 is the only release window that should be presented as confirmed.

children.text: The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 premieres in Japan on October 2, 2026 at 11:00 p.m. JST on Nippon TV's FRIDAY ANIME NIGHT block. The season is planned as a split two-cour broadcast, with the second cour beginning in April 2027. The franchise also has a separate theatrical movie scheduled for December 2026, so fans will receive both a television continuation and an original film project within the same broader period.
The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 release schedule

The first cour starts Friday, October 2, 2026 at 23:00 JST. The official production has already confirmed that Season 3 will use a split-cour structure, with its second section scheduled for April 2027. An exact episode count has not been published, so the two-cour plan should not be converted into a specific number of episodes until the production confirms it.

Crunchyroll has confirmed Season 3 for its Fall 2026 simulcast lineup across North America, Central and South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, CIS territories and the Indian Subcontinent. The Japanese broadcast begins October 2 at 11:00 p.m. JST. The official Japanese site says streaming platforms will begin carrying episodes after the TV broadcast, but Crunchyroll has not published a universal exact simulcast time.

body.alt: The Apothecary Diaries - Kusuriya no Hitorigoto

children.text: What Season 3 is about

Season 3 expands the story beyond the rear palace and into a wider political landscape. Maomao notices signs of trouble after an unusual detail at breakfast leads her toward another mystery, while Jinshi is increasingly forced to confront the responsibilities attached to his true position as the emperor's younger brother.

The official story setup also points toward signs of a national disaster and rumors surrounding a mysterious immortal-like woman. That shift gives Season 3 a broader scale than many early palace mysteries. Maomao's observational skills are still the center of the series, but the consequences of what she discovers can now extend far beyond one household or court faction.
Jinshi's role becomes more political

Jinshi can no longer remain only the elegant administrator who appears around the rear palace. His identity and status carry political obligations, and Season 3 is explicitly setting up a story where he must act with those responsibilities in mind. That creates a useful contrast with Maomao, whose instinct is usually to solve the immediate practical problem and avoid court politics whenever possible.
New character and music details

Reina Ueda is confirmed to voice Pai Nyannyan, a mysterious woman associated with the season's new storyline. Yorushika performs the opening theme, while Eve performs the ending theme, “AIYOU.” The promotional material emphasizes travel, open landscapes and a story moving beyond the familiar palace setting.
How is the December 2026 movie connected?

The Apothecary Diaries movie, titled The Deceased Empress’ Treasure, opens in Japan on December 11, 2026. It is a separate project with a completely original story based on an idea by original author Natsu Hyuga. The film should not be treated as a replacement for Season 3's second cour or as a mandatory source-material adaptation between the two television halves.
What remains unknown

The exact Season 3 episode count, final adaptation endpoint, precise April 2027 second-cour date and a universal Crunchyroll posting time remain unannounced. Confirmed details include the October 2 premiere at 11:00 p.m. JST, Crunchyroll streaming across major international regions including the Indian Subcontinent, the original movie's December 11 Japanese release, and the second cour in April 2027.

children.text: Skip and Loafer Season 2 is officially returning in April 2027. The anime's official website announced the new broadcast window on August 16, 2026 and released a teaser trailer using new footage. The update also confirms that P.A.WORKS is returning to animate the series, with Tomoyo Kurosawa back as Mitsumi Iwakura and Akinori Egoshi returning as Sosuke Shima.

The important part is that April 2027 is confirmed, but an exact premiere day is not. Any specific date beyond the month should still be treated as unconfirmed until the official site publishes the broadcast schedule. That makes this a useful point to catch up on what is actually known without turning fan predictions into release information.
Skip and Loafer Season 2 Release Date - Quick Answer
Release window: April 2027
Exact premiere day: Not announced yet
Animation studio: P.A.WORKS
Mitsumi Iwakura: Tomoyo Kurosawa
Sosuke Shima: Akinori Egoshi

Crunchyroll has also stated that it will stream the second season when it premieres. Region-specific timing can still differ, so April 2027 is the reliable global planning window until a more detailed schedule is released.
What the Season 2 Teaser Reveals

The new teaser uses fresh animation rather than simply recycling the first season. That is a reassuring sign because Skip and Loafer's appeal is difficult to sell with plot twists. Its strength comes from tiny shifts in friendships, awkward pauses, facial expressions and the way characters slowly revise what they think about one another. New footage lets the production show that the sequel is preserving that gentle observational tone.

body.alt: Skip and Loafer - Skip to Loafer

children.text: If that kind of grounded romance is what you enjoy, our
Horimiya review
looks at another school romance that works because the characters feel like people before they feel like pairings.
Is P.A.WORKS Returning?

Yes. P.A.WORKS is officially returning for Season 2. Kotomi Deai is again directing and handling series composition, while Manami Umeshita returns as character designer and chief animation director. The official staff list also includes Yoko Yonaiyama on series composition and a large group of returning production roles across animation, art, photography, sound and music.

That continuity is especially valuable for Skip and Loafer because the first season's direction was deliberately understated. The animation rarely tried to overwhelm the viewer. Instead, it gave everyday gestures and social discomfort enough room to register. A completely new team could imitate the character designs while missing the timing that made those scenes work. Keeping P.A.WORKS and major staff members lowers that risk.
Who Is Returning in the Cast?

The official announcement confirms Tomoyo Kurosawa as Mitsumi Iwakura and Akinori Egoshi as Sosuke Shima. Their performances are central to the series because Mitsumi and Shima communicate in very different ways. Mitsumi is sincere, ambitious and socially clumsy in ways she often does not notice. Shima is smoother on the surface but far more guarded about what he actually feels.

That contrast gives the story much of its tension without requiring melodrama. Mitsumi often says exactly what she means, even when her delivery is awkward. Shima often knows the socially correct thing to say, but that skill can become another way to avoid being emotionally honest. Season 2 has room to deepen that difference as their friendship becomes harder to define.
What Will Skip and Loafer Season 2 Be About?

The official site does not provide a chapter-by-chapter adaptation outline, so it is better not to present manga predictions as confirmed anime structure. What can safely be said is that the sequel continues Mitsumi's high-school life in Tokyo and the relationships that gradually formed around her during the first season. The manga remains ongoing, giving the anime substantial source material to continue exploring.

Season 1 succeeded because it understood that growing closer to people can create new uncertainty rather than solving everything. Friend groups change when two people become closer. Small jealousies feel embarrassing precisely because nobody wants to admit them. Someone who seems confident in one social setting can become insecure in another. Those are the kinds of ordinary shifts that Skip and Loafer turns into meaningful drama.
AnimeSparks explored a similar idea in
How My Dress-Up Darling Redefines Romance in Modern Anime
, where vulnerability matters more than rushing toward a confession.
Why April 2027 Is a Good Window for the Series

A spring return fits the series almost too well thematically, but the more practical advantage is that the production now has a firm window far enough in advance for viewers to rediscover Season 1. Skip and Loafer is not a show where a recap video can fully replace the experience. The details worth remembering are often not plot facts but how individual friendships formed and where each character's insecurities started to become visible.
For viewers looking for more character-driven romance during the wait, our list of
romance anime like Toradora
offers several series where personality conflicts matter as much as the central couple.
Where Will Season 2 Stream?

Crunchyroll has announced that it will stream Skip and Loafer Season 2 when the anime premieres. The exact territory list and local release times should still be checked closer to April 2027 because streaming rights can vary by region. What is confirmed now is the April 2027 television launch in Japan and Crunchyroll's participation in international distribution.
Another upcoming character-focused school series on AnimeSparks is
The Ramparts of Ice Season 2
, which returns much sooner and also builds its drama around teenagers struggling to communicate honestly.
What Is Still Unconfirmed?
The exact April 2027 premiere day
The final Season 2 episode count
The precise manga chapter where Season 2 will end
Region-specific streaming times

Those missing details are normal for a sequel still months away. The key release information is already solid: Skip and Loafer Season 2 begins broadcasting in April 2027, P.A.WORKS is returning, the principal cast is back and a teaser trailer with new footage has been released.
Final Update

Skip and Loafer Season 2 is officially scheduled for April 2027. P.A.WORKS returns with key staff members from the first season, Tomoyo Kurosawa and Akinori Egoshi return as Mitsumi and Shima, and the newly released teaser confirms that the anime is preserving the warm, subtle visual identity that made Season 1 stand out.

The exact premiere date and episode count have not yet been announced. Until the official site narrows the schedule, April 2027 is the confirmed answer, not any specific day circulating through fan speculation.

children.text: What arc does Season 4 adapt?

Season 4 centers on the Pleiades Watchtower material associated with the sixth major arc of the original story. Subaru travels through the Auguria Dunes with allies who are searching for answers that could help people affected by earlier events. The tower is not simply a new dungeon. It is tied to the Sage, old mysteries, the Books of the Dead and questions about memory and identity.

This is one of Re:Zero's most psychologically demanding stretches because Subaru's usual advantage is put under pressure. Return by Death remains central to the series, but knowledge accumulated through loops becomes less comforting when Subaru cannot fully trust his own memories, assumptions or understanding of the people around him.
Why memory matters so much this season

Memory loss is not a minor twist in this storyline. It changes the emotional rules of Re:Zero. Subaru's relationships have always depended on experiences that other characters often cannot remember because his deaths reset the world. Season 4 turns that idea back on him by challenging what happens when Subaru himself loses access to the history that normally anchors his choices.
Who is Shaula?

Shaula is one of the major new figures connected to Pleiades Watchtower and the mythology surrounding the Sage. Her behavior can be funny and disarming, but her presence also complicates the tower's history and Subaru's assumptions about people whose names have become legendary. Anime-only viewers are better served by learning those answers through the season rather than reading deep character spoilers in advance.
Where can Season 4 be streamed?

Japanese streaming includes ABEMA and d Anime Store in early slots, followed by a wide list of services such as Prime Video, Netflix, Disney+, U-NEXT, Hulu and others. International availability varies by region. Crunchyroll previously announced Season 4 streaming outside Japan, so viewers should use the platform's local schedule for exact subtitled and dubbed release times.
What comes after Season 4?

The original light novels continue beyond the Pleiades Watchtower story, so there is more material available for anime adaptation. That does not make Season 5 official. Re:Zero has enough source material to continue, but the next television season should only be treated as confirmed after the production committee announces it.

For viewers following the current anime, the important status is straightforward: Season 4 is already airing, the Loss Arc is complete, the Recapture Arc started August 12, and the full season consists of 19 episodes. The remaining story is now about how Subaru and his allies escape a situation designed to attack not just their strength, but their understanding of themselves.

children.text: Mizu is finally leaving Japan.
Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 arrives on Netflix in January 2027

, and the change of setting is much bigger than a simple backdrop swap. The new season sends Mizu to London in pursuit of the remaining men tied to her past, while the characters she left behind face a very different struggle for power in Edo.

Netflix revealed the January 2027 window alongside a new Season 2 teaser in August 2026. There is still no exact premiere day, but we now know enough about the story to see how radically the series is expanding.

Season 1 was a revenge story shaped by Mizu's position as an outsider in Edo-period Japan. Season 2 asks what happens when that outsider enters the world she has spent much of her life associating with the people she hates.
Spoiler warning:
this article discusses the ending of
Blue Eye Samurai
Season 1 and officially revealed details about Season 2.
When Is Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Coming Out?
Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 will premiere on Netflix in January 2027.
Netflix has not announced the exact day yet.

That is the most important distinction for anyone searching for a release date: January 2027 is confirmed, but any specific January date circulating before Netflix announces one should be treated cautiously.

The wait has been long. Season 1 premiered in November 2023, and Netflix officially renewed the series the following month. The production's highly detailed animation helps explain why this is not the kind of show that can simply return every year.
For viewers building a Netflix watchlist while waiting, AnimeSparks also has a guide to the
best anime on Netflix worth watching
, covering a broader mix of action, drama and fantasy.
Where Will Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Stream?
Season 2 is a
Netflix original and will stream on Netflix
. Season 1 remains available there as well, making it easy to revisit Mizu's journey before the new episodes arrive.

children.text: Netflix has not yet confirmed the Season 2 episode count. Season 1 had eight episodes, but that does not mean Season 2 is guaranteed to use the same structure.
Why Is Mizu Going to London?
The Season 1 finale completely redirects Mizu's revenge quest.

Mizu spent the first season hunting the four white men who were illegally in Japan around the time of her birth. Her hatred of those men is inseparable from the prejudice she endured because of her mixed heritage and blue eyes.
By the finale, Abijah Fowler is beaten but still useful. Instead of killing him, Mizu keeps him alive because he possesses information she needs. Fowler identifies
Skeffington and Routely
as two remaining targets and tells her where they can be found: London.
Netflix's official Season 2 material confirms that this is where the story picks up. Mizu is sailing toward England, with her bloody quest continuing in London.
That decision changes almost everything about the series.
London Is More Than a New Setting
The smartest thing Season 2 can do with London is make it challenge Mizu's worldview rather than simply giving her European enemies to cut through.
Co-creator Amber Noizumi has already pointed toward that idea, asking what Mizu will think of Western culture when she is suddenly immersed in it and how Europeans will react to her.

That is crucial because Mizu has spent her life being treated as visibly different in Japan. Her blue eyes mark her before she speaks. She hides her gender and controls how the world perceives her because survival has taught her to treat identity as armor.
In London, the social rules change.

Mizu may still be an outsider, but she will be an outsider for different reasons. The people around her will not share the exact prejudices or assumptions she grew up navigating in Japan. At the same time, seventeenth-century England is hardly going to become a welcoming refuge.
Season 2 therefore has the opportunity to make Mizu confront a difficult truth: the people she has reduced to symbols of her suffering are part of a much larger world she has never actually seen.
That does not invalidate her revenge. It complicates it.
What Does the Season 2 Teaser Show?

Netflix's August 2026 teaser emphasizes the journey itself as well as the destination. Mizu's voyage toward London is dangerous, and the footage reinforces that Season 2 is not abandoning the physical brutality that defined the first season.
But the most interesting promise is not simply another collection of sword fights.
Netflix describes Mizu as facing
new friends, old foes and her own demons
in London. That last phrase matters. Season 1 repeatedly showed that revenge is not a clean mission Mizu can complete without damaging herself and the people who care about her.

London puts distance between her and almost every relationship that softened her during Season 1. That isolation could make her more dangerous—but it could also force her to understand what those relationships meant.
Is Abijah Fowler Returning?
The Season 1 ending leaves Fowler alive and aboard the ship with Mizu, so his role remains central to the London setup.
Fowler is not a conventional traveling companion. He is a prisoner, an enemy and a source of information Mizu cannot easily replace. That creates an inherently unstable relationship.
He knows more about the men Mizu is hunting and about the circumstances surrounding her birth. Mizu knows he is manipulative, violent and dangerous. Neither has any reason to trust the other.
That tension could become one of Season 2's best dynamics because Fowler is useful precisely as long as Mizu believes he knows something she needs.
Who Are Skeffington and Routely?
Skeffington and Routely are the names Fowler gives Mizu when explaining where her remaining targets can be found.

For now, viewers should resist treating every theory about them as established fact. Netflix has confirmed Mizu's London revenge story, but it has not publicly revealed every detail about these men, their positions, or how Mizu will reach them.
What matters is that London turns the revenge list from an abstract goal into a destination.
Season 1 was about fighting toward Fowler. Season 2 can now ask whether reaching the other men actually gives Mizu the answers she expects.
What Happens to Akemi in Season 2?
Mizu's departure does not mean the story is abandoning Japan.
Netflix confirms that
Akemi and Taigen will navigate Edo Castle under a dangerous new shogun
. This gives Season 2 two very different arenas: Mizu's violent search in London and a political struggle inside Edo.
Akemi may be the character best positioned to carry that second storyline.
Her Season 1 arc was about rejecting the limited futures other people chose for her. By the finale, she no longer wants merely to escape power. She wants to possess it.

That transformation makes her a fascinating counterpoint to Mizu. Both women resist systems that restrict them, but they increasingly use opposite methods. Mizu cuts through obstacles. Akemi learns to manipulate the structures around her.
AnimeSparks explored another deceptively dangerous historical heroine in our analysis of
knowledge as power in Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia
, and Akemi's political evolution makes for an interesting comparison: neither character needs to dominate a battlefield to become dangerous.
What Happens to Taigen?
Taigen remains in Japan, where Netflix says he will navigate Edo Castle alongside Akemi.

That is a significant change from his relationship with Mizu in Season 1. Their rivalry gradually became respect, attraction and a strange kind of companionship, but Mizu ultimately chose revenge over the possibility of a different life.
Season 2 can now develop Taigen without making every decision revolve around chasing Mizu.
His proximity to Akemi also reopens one of the show's most complicated relationships. They were once supposed to marry, but both have changed dramatically since that arrangement collapsed.
The question is no longer simply whether Taigen loves Akemi or Mizu. It is what kind of person he becomes when honor, romance and status stop giving him an obvious path forward.
Where Is Ringo in Season 2?
Ringo's Season 2 direction sounds quieter but may be just as important.
Netflix says
Ringo is searching for new purpose

Ringo began as someone desperate to attach himself to greatness. He saw Mizu as a master and wanted to become part of her story. Over time, however, he also became one of the few people willing to challenge what her revenge was turning her into.
With Mizu gone, Ringo has to define greatness for himself.
That is a healthier and potentially more mature direction than simply sending him across the world to follow her again.
Will Mizu and Taigen Reunite in Season 2?
Netflix has not confirmed when—or whether—Mizu and Taigen reunite during Season 2.
The official setup deliberately separates them: Mizu is in London, while Taigen remains involved with events at Edo Castle.

That distance may be narratively useful. Their relationship developed under constant danger, rivalry and physical proximity. Separating them gives both characters room to change independently before any eventual reunion.
A reunion is certainly possible, but presenting it as confirmed would go beyond what Netflix has announced.
Who Is Returning in the Cast?
Netflix's current Season 2 information lists
Maya Erskine returning as Mizu
, alongside
Brenda Song as Akemi, Darren Barnet as Taigen and Masi Oka as Ringo

Season 1 also featured Kenneth Branagh as Abijah Fowler, George Takei as Seki, Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa as the Swordmaker, Randall Park as Heiji Shindo, Stephanie Hsu as Ise, Ming-Na Wen as Madame Kaji, Harry Shum Jr. as Takayoshi and Mark Dacascos as Chiaki.
Not every Season 1 character should automatically be assumed to have a major Season 2 role. The new London setting naturally creates room for a different supporting cast.
Is the Same Creative Team Returning?
Yes.
Amber Noizumi and Michael Green
remain the creators and writers, and they executive produce alongside Erwin Stoff.
Jane Wu
remains supervising director and producer, while
Blue Spirit
is the animation studio behind the series.
That continuity matters because
Blue Eye Samurai

has such a specific visual identity. Its action feels choreographed with live-action physicality, but its environments and faces take advantage of animation's ability to exaggerate composition, light and movement.
If sword-focused action is what brought you to the series, our ranking of the
strongest anime swordsmen
explores how very different franchises build sword fighters around technique, mythology and raw power.
Why Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Could Feel Very Different
Season 1's Japan was not just scenery. Social class, gender, isolationism, race and political hierarchy shaped almost every character's choices.
Moving half of the story to London means the writers cannot simply reproduce those pressures with European architecture in the background.
That is exactly why the new season is exciting.

Mizu has mastered surviving the world that created her. She understands how to disguise herself, how men underestimate women, how samurai measure status and how violence functions within the society she knows.
London takes away that familiarity.

She will have to read new customs, new power structures and potentially new forms of prejudice while pursuing people who may understand Europe far better than she does. Even her swordsmanship exists in a place where firearms and different fighting traditions change the practical rules of confrontation.
The result could make Season 2 feel less like a repetition of Season 1 and more like the next stage of Mizu's identity crisis.
Blue Eye Samurai Has Already Been Renewed for Season 3
Season 2 is not being positioned as the end of the story.
Netflix has confirmed that
Blue Eye Samurai will conclude with Season 3 in 2028
. That is unusually useful information because it gives the story a visible endpoint: Mizu's revenge saga is being built toward a planned conclusion rather than an indefinite run.
That also changes how we should think about Season 2.
London does not need to resolve every mystery. It needs to transform the revenge quest enough to set up its final consequences.

The strongest possibility is that Mizu discovers revenge is more complicated than the list of names she has carried in her head. Season 1 already planted that idea. Seasons 2 and 3 now have room to finish it.
What Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Needs to Answer
The obvious questions concern Mizu's remaining targets: Who exactly are Skeffington and Routely? What do they know about her birth? Can Fowler be trusted long enough to lead her to them?
But the emotional questions are more interesting.

What does Mizu actually want if revenge stops giving her identity? What happens when she encounters people in Europe who do not fit the monstrous image she has built? How far will Akemi go for political power? Can Taigen build an identity that is not based on status or defeating Mizu? What does Ringo consider greatness when his master is gone?
Those questions are why
Blue Eye Samurai
works as more than an action series.
Like the best historical animation, its violence is tied to the world that produces it. AnimeSparks' piece on
The Elusive Samurai's darker historical reality
looks at a very different period and style, but both stories use historical upheaval to strip away the comforting idea that skill with a sword guarantees control over one's life.
What We Know About Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 So Far
The confirmed picture is now fairly clear.
Season 2 arrives in January 2027 on Netflix.

Mizu travels to London to continue hunting the men connected to her past. Akemi and Taigen remain in Japan and face danger at Edo Castle under a new shogun. Ringo searches for purpose. Maya Erskine, Brenda Song, Darren Barnet and Masi Oka are among the returning voices, and the core creative team remains in place.
What we do
not
have yet is an exact January premiere date or a confirmed episode count.

More importantly, Season 2 is no longer just a promise that Mizu has “more blood to spill.” It has a shape. London will take the character who has spent her life believing her appearance makes her monstrous and place her inside the culture she associates with that difference.
That could make the next chapter more than a bigger revenge story.
It could force Mizu to decide whether revenge is something she wants to finish—or the only identity she knows how to inhabit.

children.text: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 now has an exact release date. CD PROJEKT RED announced on August 21, 2026 that the new anime will premiere exclusively on Netflix on October 20. The announcement arrived with a new trailer and confirmed that Studio TRIGGER's return to Night City will be a 10-episode standalone story with an entirely new cast rather than a direct continuation of David Martinez's arc.

That distinction matters for anyone searching for a conventional 'Season 2.' Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is the next anime in the same universe, but its creators have consistently described it as a fresh story. David's story remains complete. The sequel instead uses Night City itself as the connective tissue, following new people who are caught in the same violent system of corporations, cyberware, ambition and survival.
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Release Date - Quick Answer
Netflix premiere: October 20, 2026
Episode count: 10 episodes
Animation studio: TRIGGER
Format: New standalone story set in the Cyberpunk 2077 universe
Director: Kai Ikarashi

There is no longer any need to rely on a broad Fall 2026 estimate. October 20 is the official Netflix date announced by CD PROJEKT RED. As always, local availability pages can differ slightly in how they display release timing, but the global promotional announcement gives viewers a clear date to work with.
What the New Trailer Confirms

The latest trailer is built around revenge and redemption, two themes that CD PROJEKT RED explicitly highlighted in its release-date announcement. Rather than trying to recreate David and Lucy's tragedy with replacement characters, the footage suggests a different group of edgerunners whose lives collide for their own reasons. The creative team is still using the same basic strength of the first anime: Night City is not just a backdrop. It is a machine that rewards desperation, punishes attachment and constantly tempts people to trade more of themselves for power.

That makes the sequel especially interesting for viewers who like science fiction where technology changes identity rather than simply giving characters cooler weapons. AnimeSparks has explored that same idea from a different angle in our
Ghost in the Shell 2026 analysis
, which looks at how cybernetic bodies reshape questions about selfhood.
Is This a Direct Continuation of the First Anime?

No. The safest description is a standalone second installment in the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime line. CD PROJEKT RED has repeatedly described the project as a new story with a brand-new cast. That means viewers should not expect the plot to undo the original ending or turn David's fate into a cliffhanger that was secretly waiting for a sequel.

This is a smart creative choice. The first series became memorable because it committed to consequences. A conventional sequel could weaken that finality. By moving to new characters, Edgerunners 2 can preserve the emotional weight of the original while exploring another corner of the same city. Night City has more than enough gangs, corporations, mercenaries, fixers and ordinary people to support multiple tragedies without forcing every story into one family tree.
Who Is Making Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2?

Studio TRIGGER is returning, which is arguably the most important continuity point for the anime. Kai Ikarashi is directing, with Kanno Ichigo as lead character designer. Bartosz Sztybor returns as showrunner, story writer and producer, while Masahiko Otsuka is also involved in the screenplay adaptation. The team combines people who understand the visual language of the original with a new director who can give the sequel its own rhythm.

TRIGGER's role matters because Edgerunners depends on extreme contrasts: fluorescent color against brutal violence, exaggerated motion against quiet emotional scenes, and comedy that can turn tragic in minutes. The studio made the first anime feel unmistakably connected to Cyberpunk 2077 without looking like a game cutscene. A return from the same studio gives the second series a strong chance of keeping that identity.
What Is the Story About?

The official description keeps major plot details deliberately broad. What is confirmed is that the series follows a fresh cast whose paths intersect as they fight their own battles across Night City. The creators describe the story as raw and human, centered on revenge and redemption. That language suggests the sequel will again focus on personal consequences rather than turning into a lore-heavy tour of the Cyberpunk universe.

The official Cyberpunk site has also begun introducing new characters, including Weak, a veteran edgerunner living in the shadow of his former reputation; D, a talented nomad netrunner driven by revenge; Roman, a young filmmaker obsessed with documenting reality; and Talia, a fiercely independent woman shaped by Maelstrom's violent chrome culture. These descriptions already show how different their motivations are from David's rise through the underworld.
Why the 10-Episode Format Is Good News

The first Edgerunners also used a compact 10-episode structure, and the same length suits this kind of story. Night City narratives become less effective when every danger turns into a long arc with endless recovery time. A shorter run forces relationships, betrayals and consequences to move quickly. It also reduces the temptation to pad the story with side missions that would feel natural in a game but unnecessary in a television drama.
For viewers looking for more tightly written science fiction while waiting, our
Steins;Gate retrospective
is another example of an anime where the emotional cost of technology matters more than spectacle alone.
Where Will Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Stream?

Netflix is the confirmed exclusive home for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. CD PROJEKT RED's August 21 announcement specifically says the series premieres on Netflix on October 20. No alternate broadcast network has been announced as a parallel home for the new anime.
If you are building a watch list around the platform, AnimeSparks also keeps a broader
best anime on Netflix guide
covering series worth watching beyond the Cyberpunk universe.
Final Update

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 premieres October 20, 2026 on Netflix. It is a 10-episode standalone story from CD PROJEKT RED and Studio TRIGGER, directed by Kai Ikarashi and built around a completely new cast. The latest trailer emphasizes revenge, redemption and another violent collision of lives inside Night City.

The key thing to remember is that this is not a resurrection of the first season's plot. David's story remains finished. Edgerunners 2 is using the same world to tell a new tragedy, which gives the creators freedom to surprise viewers without weakening what made the original ending work.

children.text: One Piece Film God Valley is officially scheduled for a Summer 2027 theatrical release in Japan. The movie was announced as part of One Piece's 30th-anniversary year, while a second film titled One Piece Film BAAD is planned for 2029. The title immediately points toward one of the most important historical events in the series, but the production has not yet released a full synopsis, exact premiere day or international theatrical schedule.
One Piece Film God Valley release date

The official One Piece announcement confirms Summer 2027 for Japanese theaters. It does not narrow that window to a particular month or day. Japan will mark the manga's 30th anniversary on July 22, 2027, which explains why the film is being positioned as an anniversary project, but that anniversary date should not be mistaken for the movie's confirmed opening day.
What is the God Valley Incident?

God Valley is a legendary event from One Piece history that took place decades before Luffy's journey. It is connected to the Rocks Pirates, Gol D. Roger, Monkey D. Garp and the World Government. The incident became famous because Roger and Garp were involved in stopping the threat associated with Rocks D. Xebec, even though the full circumstances were hidden from the public inside the story.

That history matters because several of the most influential figures in the modern One Piece world were tied to Rocks or to the generation that confronted him. A film focused on God Valley therefore has the potential to connect pirate history, Marine history and the secrets of the World Government in a way most previous One Piece movies have not.

body.alt: One Piece God Valley Incident - Rocks Pirates, Garp, and Roger

children.text: Will Rocks D. Xebec, Roger and Garp be in the movie?

The film's title makes the God Valley setting official, and the announcement material directly associates the project with the historical incident. Rocks, Roger and Garp are the central names fans connect with that event. However, the production has not yet published a complete character roster or detailed synopsis, so AnimeSparks will avoid treating every manga participant as a confirmed movie character until the staff reveals more.
Is One Piece Film God Valley canon?

The God Valley Incident itself is part of the manga's canon history. That does not automatically make every scene created for a theatrical adaptation canon. One Piece films often use canonical characters, concepts or information while telling a movie-specific version of events. Until Eiichiro Oda or the production committee clarifies how the film should be treated, the safest description is that the movie is based around a canonical event rather than declaring every film-original detail manga canon.
How could the movie fit with the manga?

God Valley has been revealed gradually through flashbacks, character histories and later story developments rather than through one continuous early chapter. That gives a movie an unusual opportunity to present the incident as a more unified narrative. It also creates a challenge: the anime film cannot safely reveal information the manga has not yet chosen to explain unless that material is coordinated directly with Oda and the manga's publication schedule.

For anime-only viewers, the movie may therefore work best if it explains enough historical context to stand alone without assuming detailed knowledge of every late-series revelation. For manga readers, the appeal is different: they will be watching to see which pieces of the long-discussed incident become fully dramatized.
What is One Piece Film BAAD?

Film BAAD is a separate One Piece theatrical project officially scheduled for 2029, the year the television anime reaches its 30th anniversary. Its story has not been announced. The title image was drawn by Oda, but there is currently no basis for claiming that BAAD is a direct sequel to God Valley or that the two films form one story.
When will the trailer, cast and international dates be announced?

The next useful updates will be a full trailer, director and staff credits, voice-cast announcements, an exact Japanese premiere date and overseas distribution plans. One Piece movies commonly receive international releases, but previous franchise patterns are not proof of a specific country or date. Those details should be added only when licensed distributors announce them.

For now, the confirmed status is strong enough to separate fact from rumor: One Piece Film God Valley is real, it opens in Japan in Summer 2027, it is tied to the manga's 30th-anniversary year, and Film BAAD follows as a separate movie in 2029. The exact story, canon treatment, staff, runtime and international release calendar remain open.

children.text: For decades,
Hajime no Ippo

has been one of the strangest omissions on English-language manga shelves. George Morikawa's boxing epic has run since 1989, crossed 100 million copies worldwide, inspired multiple anime series and built an enormous international fanbase—yet English readers have never had an official physical edition to collect.
That is finally changing.
At
Anime NYC 2026
, Kodansha USA announced that
Hajime no Ippo: Fighting Spirit!
will receive its
first official English print release in fall 2027
. The series will be published as premium paperback omnibuses, with
three Japanese volumes collected in each English book

For longtime Ippo fans, this is not a routine license announcement. It removes one of the biggest barriers between an all-time sports manga and the English-speaking audience that has spent years asking for it.
There is also one important clarification:
this is a manga announcement, not a new Hajime no Ippo anime season.
No Season 4 or new anime project was announced as part of Kodansha USA's Anime NYC news.
When Does the Hajime no Ippo English Omnibus Come Out?
Kodansha USA has announced a
fall 2027
release window for the first
Hajime no Ippo: Fighting Spirit!
English omnibus.
An exact release date has not been announced yet.
Each premium paperback will collect
three volumes of the original Japanese manga
, giving new readers a faster way to move through the early story while making the enormous series somewhat more practical to collect.
The English title being used is
Hajime no Ippo: Fighting Spirit!
, connecting the manga to the name many Western anime viewers already recognize.
What Exactly Did Kodansha Announce?
The announcement came during Kodansha USA's Anime NYC 2026 panel as part of its fall 2027 print lineup.

body.alt: Hajime no Ippo - Hajime no Ippo

children.text: The publisher described the release as the series'
English print debut
and confirmed the premium 3-in-1 paperback format.
That distinction matters because
Hajime no Ippo
has been available officially in English digitally through K MANGA. The 2027 release is historic because it finally puts Morikawa's series into physical English volumes.

For a manga with well over 140 Japanese volumes, the omnibus format also makes obvious practical sense. Releasing three volumes at a time reduces the number of books required to catch up while still giving collectors a substantial physical edition.
Why Has Hajime no Ippo Taken So Long to Get an English Print Release?
Kodansha has not presented one single official explanation for every year the series remained absent from English print, so claims about the exact reason should be treated carefully.
But the challenge is easy to understand.
Hajime no Ippo
is enormous.
The manga began serialization in
Weekly Shonen Magazine
in
and has continued for decades. Licensing a series of that size means committing to a catalog far larger than most new manga releases.

That makes the 3-in-1 format especially significant. Kodansha is not approaching Ippo as a standard one-volume-at-a-time launch. The omnibus strategy gives the publisher a more realistic way to move through decades of material.
What Will the First Omnibus Cover?
Kodansha has confirmed that each omnibus contains three original volumes. That means the opening release should take readers back to the very beginning of
Ippo Makunouchi's boxing journey
Ippo starts as a shy high-school student who helps his mother with the family's fishing boat business and endures bullying without knowing how to fight back. His life changes after professional boxer
Mamoru Takamura
intervenes and brings him to Kamogawa Boxing Gym.
What begins as curiosity quickly becomes something deeper. Ippo discovers both a talent for punching and a question that will define his life:
what does it mean to be strong?

That question is why the early manga remains so effective decades later. The series is not simply about watching Ippo acquire stronger techniques. It is about the cost of improvement and the way his understanding of strength keeps changing.
AnimeSparks explored that side of the series in
Hajime no Ippo Shows What It Really Costs To Improve
, which makes a useful companion read for anyone returning to the story before the new editions arrive.
Is This a New Hajime no Ippo Anime Announcement?
No.
Kodansha USA's announcement is for the
English-language physical manga release
. It does not confirm
Hajime no Ippo
Season 4, a reboot, a movie or another anime adaptation.
That clarification is important because the series' long anime absence means any major Ippo announcement immediately generates speculation about a return.
The most recent television anime,
Hajime no Ippo: Rising
, aired from 2013 to 2014. More than a decade later, there is still substantial manga material that has never been animated.
The new English edition may expose the series to more readers and renew international attention, but that is not the same thing as an anime production announcement.
Does the New Release Make Hajime no Ippo Season 4 More Likely?
There is no official evidence that the English print license is directly connected to a new anime season.
It is tempting to connect the two because publishers often benefit from cross-media attention, but doing so here would be speculation.
What we can say is that
Hajime no Ippo

remains commercially and culturally significant. Kodansha's decision to launch a premium English omnibus line decades into the manga's run demonstrates that the publisher still sees international demand for Morikawa's work.
Whether that demand contributes to a future anime revival is a separate question.
Until an anime committee, studio, broadcaster or official
Hajime no Ippo
channel announces something, fans should treat Season 4 posts on social media cautiously.
Why This Release Is Such a Big Deal for English Manga Readers
Some manga licenses are exciting because the series is new.
Hajime no Ippo
is exciting for the opposite reason.
English readers have been waiting for this one for decades.

The series belongs in the same conversation as the defining sports manga of its era, yet physical English collectors have never been able to build an official Ippo shelf. Fans who discovered the story through the anime often had to choose between stopping where the adaptation ended or finding another way to continue the manga.
The new omnibuses finally create an official physical path from Chapter 1 onward.
And unlike a short prestige reprint, this is a series whose scale can turn the collection itself into a long-term project.
Why Hajime no Ippo Still Works After More Than 35 Years
The easiest explanation is that boxing gives Morikawa an almost perfect framework for character writing.

Every opponent can represent a different answer to the same question Ippo keeps asking about strength. Some fighters are technically gifted. Some are physically monstrous. Some are desperate. Some are disciplined. Some fight because boxing is the only place where their lives make sense.
That makes matches feel personal even when the championship stakes are familiar.
The series also understands something great sports anime repeatedly rediscover: training only matters if improvement has a cost.
That is part of what makes
Haikyu!!
compelling too. AnimeSparks' essay on
why Haikyu!! is about effort without a promise of greatness
explores a similar idea from volleyball's perspective. Working harder can change you without guaranteeing that you win.
Ippo lives inside that tension.
How Much Hajime no Ippo Is There to Collect?
A lot.
That is both the attraction and the intimidating part of this announcement. The Japanese manga has been running since 1989 and has accumulated well over a hundred volumes.
At three original volumes per omnibus, an eventual complete English collection would still require a very large number of books.

Kodansha has not announced a complete long-term release schedule covering the entire Japanese run, so readers should not assume how quickly later omnibuses will arrive. What is confirmed is the format and the fall 2027 launch.
The best approach is to treat the first omnibus as the beginning of a major publishing project rather than expecting the English edition to catch Japan immediately.
What Should New Readers Expect From Hajime no Ippo?
Do not approach it expecting a nonstop sequence of championship fights.

The boxing is excellent, but the series earns those matches through training, rivalry and character relationships. Ippo's progression is gradual. Techniques have to be learned. Physical weaknesses matter. Damage matters. Confidence matters.
And losing can permanently change the direction of a fighter's career.
That grounded approach is one reason the series has remained influential while sports-anime trends have changed around it.

If your entry point is newer sports anime, Ippo may feel slower at first. Give the gym dynamics and early training room to work. Morikawa is building a cast that will matter for hundreds of chapters, not simply rushing Ippo toward his first major opponent.
For another character-first sports series, AnimeSparks' feature on
why Run with the Wind deserves more fans
shows how competition becomes more powerful when the people matter more than the scoreboard.
How Does Ippo Compare With Modern Sports Anime?
Modern hits such as
Blue Lock
often emphasize spectacle, individual ambition and rapid psychological confrontation. Ippo comes from a different tradition, but that contrast makes it more interesting rather than less relevant.
Our
Blue Lock Season 3 guide
shows how the Neo Egoist League turns improvement into an almost ruthless marketplace of individual value.
Hajime no Ippo
asks a quieter question: how much of yourself are you willing to rebuild just to become a little stronger than yesterday?
Both are obsessed with improvement. They simply define its meaning differently.
What We Still Don't Know
Several details remain unconfirmed after the Anime NYC announcement:
The exact fall 2027 release date
The final retail price
The first omnibus ISBN and retailer preorder date
The complete physical specifications
Whether the books will include bonus or color material
The release cadence after the first omnibus
How far Kodansha currently plans to take the English print line
None of those unknowns change the significance of the announcement itself.
Hajime no Ippo Is Finally Getting the English Edition It Deserves
There is something fitting about
Hajime no Ippo
reaching English print this late.
The series itself is obsessed with persistence.
Ippo does not become meaningful because success arrives quickly. He becomes meaningful because improvement is slow, painful and uncertain, and he keeps returning to the gym anyway.
English readers have had their own much less dramatic version of that wait. For years, an official physical release seemed increasingly unlikely simply because the manga kept getting longer.
Now Kodansha is taking it on.
Hajime no Ippo: Fighting Spirit! begins its official English print run in fall 2027 as a premium 3-in-1 omnibus series.
There is no new anime announcement attached to the news, but the manga release alone is historic enough.
After more than three decades, Ippo is finally stepping into the English-language ring in print.

children.text: Reincarnated as a Sword
is finally returning after a four-year wait, and Season 2 is sending Fran and Teacher into a much more dangerous kind of dungeon.
Season 2 begins its Japanese streaming run on ABEMA on September 30, 2026 at 24:30, one week before the television broadcast starts on October 7.
That distinction matters. September 30 is the confirmed
ABEMA early-streaming premiere
, while TOKYO MX and ABC TV begin broadcasting the season on October 7. BS Asahi and AT-X follow on October 9.
The latest trailer also makes the new season's direction clear. Fran and Teacher are heading toward the mysterious
Floating Island
, where an army of undead monsters and a powerful Lich turn their next adventure into something much darker than a routine guild quest.
Reincarnated as a Sword Season 2 Release Date — Quick Answer
Reincarnated as a Sword Season 2 premieres September 30, 2026 on ABEMA in Japan.
The Japanese television broadcast begins October 7 on TOKYO MX and ABC TV, followed by BS Asahi and AT-X on October 9.
The official schedule currently lists:
ABEMA: September 30 at 24:30, with one-week advance exclusive streaming
TOKYO MX: October 7 at 24:00
ABC TV: October 7 at 26:15
BS Asahi: October 9 at 23:00
AT-X: October 9 at 21:00
Broadcast and streaming times can still change, so the official anime site remains the final authority for the Japanese schedule.
For fans building a larger fantasy watchlist around the fall season, AnimeSparks' ranking of the
best isekai anime to watch in 2026
is a useful place to find more series while waiting for Fran's return.
What Is Reincarnated as a Sword Season 2 About?
Season 2 continues Fran's journey to become strong enough to achieve the
evolution of the Black Cat tribe
, with Teacher committed to helping her reach that goal.
After building a reputation as an adventurer in Alessa, Fran and Teacher set their sights on the port town of
Dars
. Their journey changes when they discover an enormous island floating in the sky.
There they meet
Jean Doobie
, a necromancer attempting to completely conquer the Floating Island. Fran and Teacher accept his request to join the expedition.
The problem is that the island is not an ordinary ruin.
It is a brutal dungeon crawling with
undead magical beasts
, and the new trailer shows the pair facing overwhelming numbers of enemies before confronting a Lich powerful enough to headline the new key visual.
Season 1 was already willing to put Fran in genuine danger. Season 2 appears ready to increase both the scale and the horror of those encounters.
The Floating Island Is Season 2's First Major Destination
The Floating Island gives the sequel a strong opening setting because it combines nearly everything
Reincarnated as a Sword
does well: exploration, monsters, skill progression and Fran's refusal to retreat from opponents stronger than she is.

The official introduction describes Jean as seeking the island's complete conquest and Fran joining him inside its dungeon. The first promotional video emphasized the army of the dead waiting there, while the second PV goes further by showing the Lich and teasing a connection between the mysterious
Nameless
and the island itself.
That last detail suggests the dungeon will not function merely as a place for Fran to grind levels. There is a mystery underneath the combat.
For a series whose protagonist can absorb magic stones and acquire skills, a monster-filled dungeon is also the perfect environment to test Teacher's unusual progression system.
Who Is Jean Doobie?
Jean Doobie
, voiced by
Yuma Uchida
, is one of Season 2's most important new allies.
The official character profile identifies Jean as a high-ranking necromancer known as a
Nethermancer
, capable of creating an army from corpses. His nickname, “Massacre,” makes him sound like a villain Fran should be fighting rather than someone she should accompany.
He is a B-rank adventurer whose research into necromancy brings him to the Floating Island dungeon.

That makes Jean an immediately useful addition to the cast. Fran's morality is usually direct: protect people who deserve protection and cut down those who abuse the weak. A necromancer surrounded by corpses introduces a character whose powers look sinister without automatically defining his intentions.
The Lich Is the New Enemy to Watch
The first Season 2 key visual places
Fran and Teacher directly against the Lich
, making the new enemy one of the clearest threats revealed so far.
The Lich is voiced by veteran actor
Sho Hayami

PV2 shows the undead threat on a much larger scale, with Fran fighting through numerous dead monsters before the Lich confrontation. That makes the enemy important not simply because of individual power, but because of the environment surrounding the battle.

Fran is at her most exciting when she has to combine her own speed and instincts with Teacher's enormous collection of abilities. An enemy associated with undead forces creates opportunities for the anime to push that partnership rather than reducing the encounter to a simple sword duel.
Who Is Nameless?
Another new figure receiving attention in the Season 2 promotion is
Nameless
, voiced by
Shiori Izawa

The latest promotional material specifically hints at a connection between Nameless and the Floating Island. The official campaign has not explained every part of that relationship yet, and that mystery is worth preserving rather than filling it with source-material spoilers.

For anime-only viewers, the important point is that the Floating Island has history. Its undead army and Lich are not necessarily isolated obstacles; the season is already suggesting that the dungeon's past matters.
Fran's Real Goal Is Still Evolution
The spectacle of a floating dungeon can make it easy to forget why Fran is traveling in the first place.
Her goal is
evolution

Fran belongs to the Black Cat tribe, and her desire to overcome the limits placed on her people gives her progression more emotional weight than simply becoming an increasingly overpowered adventurer.

Teacher's own priorities have also changed because of that goal. He began his new life trying to understand what he was and how his strange abilities worked. Once Fran became his wielder, his purpose became inseparable from helping her survive and grow.
That relationship is the heart of the series.
It is also what distinguishes
Reincarnated as a Sword
from many reincarnation stories built around a single overwhelmingly powerful lead. AnimeSparks' list of the
most overpowered isekai protagonists
is a fun comparison because Teacher possesses absurd potential, yet the story works by making that power part of a partnership rather than a one-man fantasy.
Fran and Teacher Are Still the Reason the Series Works

body.alt: Official Reincarnated as a Sword promotional visual featuring Fran and Teacher
body.insertAfterHeading: ## Fran and Teacher Are Still the Reason the Series Works

children.text: The title's joke is that the protagonist reincarnated as a sword. The story's emotional hook is that he became
Fran's sword

Teacher can acquire skills by absorbing magic stones and can move through telekinesis, but Fran gives those abilities direction. Meanwhile, Teacher gives a former slave something she was denied for most of her life: support without ownership.
He is protective to the point of being openly parental, but the best moments in their relationship come when he understands that protecting Fran cannot mean preventing her from taking risks.
She wants to become stronger. That means she has to fight.

Season 2's Floating Island setup appears designed to stress that balance. Teacher has more tools than ever, but Fran is entering a dungeon where their accumulated strength may not be enough to make every battle safe.
Which Voice Actors Are Returning for Season 2?
The core cast returns with
Shinichiro Miki as Teacher
and
Ai Kakuma as Fran
The currently announced cast also includes:
Hiroki Goto as Urushi
Yuma Uchida as Jean Doobie
Shiori Izawa as Nameless
Sho Hayami as the Lich
Miki and Kakuma's chemistry is especially important because Teacher and Fran's conversations have to sell both sides of their relationship: combat coordination and an increasingly family-like bond.
Is Studio C2C Returning?
Yes.
C2C
returns as the animation studio for Season 2.
Shinji Ishihira
is directing,
Takahiro Nagano
handles series composition and scripts,
Atsuko Saito
is character designer, and
Yasuharu Takanashi
returns on music.
The broader staff includes action directors Rino Isago, Satoshi Sakai and Shunya Nitta, with Hinokuni Animation involved in 3DCG work.

The continuity matters. Season 1's appeal depended heavily on giving Fran's swordplay enough speed and weight to make her feel dangerous while still preserving the expressive comedy between fights. The Season 2 trailers suggest the production is aiming for the same balance on a larger battlefield.
What Are the Season 2 Opening and Ending Songs?
Season 2's opening theme is
“DREAM OF BUTTERFLY” by FZMZ
. The song is previewed in the second promotional video.
The ending theme is
“Baribari Buddy” by HANABIE.
The two choices give the sequel a more aggressive musical identity, which fits a trailer dominated by undead hordes, aerial movement and the Lich battle.
Where Can You Watch Reincarnated as a Sword Season 2?
In Japan,
ABEMA has the one-week advance exclusive streaming window beginning September 30
The TV broadcast then begins October 7.

For international viewers, HIDIVE previously announced that it acquired Season 2 for its 2026 lineup. Exact regional availability and episode timing can differ by territory, so viewers should check HIDIVE's schedule closer to the premiere rather than assuming the Japanese ABEMA time applies worldwide.
What Happened at the End of Season 1?
Season 1 established Fran as a legitimate adventurer rather than simply a rescued girl carrying an unusual weapon.

Her partnership with Teacher grew through battles, dungeon exploration and encounters with people who either respected or underestimated her. By the end, Fran's desire to evolve had become the clearest long-term objective driving their travels.
Season 2 does not reset that progress. The official introduction specifically describes Fran as having made a name for herself through numerous quests before setting out toward Dars.
That continuity is important. Fran is stronger now, but the Floating Island exists to show that the world still contains threats capable of pushing her beyond what she has already learned.
How Does Reincarnated as a Sword Compare With Other Isekai?
The unusual reincarnation gimmick is what gets attention, but it is not what gives the series staying power.
The better idea is the partnership.

Teacher is technically the reincarnated protagonist, yet Fran is often the character whose growth drives the plot. That creates a structure where power acquisition and character development do not belong to exactly the same person.

It also keeps Teacher's strength from becoming completely self-indulgent. He can collect skills and become stronger, but his most meaningful victories are the ones that help Fran become capable of standing on her own.
That makes the series an interesting neighbor to bigger isekai franchises such as
Mushoku Tensei
. AnimeSparks' breakdown of
Mushoku Tensei's Seven Great Powers
shows a world obsessed with formal rankings and legendary strength;
Reincarnated as a Sword
makes its progression more personal by tying Fran's strength to a cultural barrier she desperately wants to break.
Why Season 2 Has Taken Four Years

Season 1 aired from October through December 2022, and the sequel was announced after its finale. The wait has therefore been unusually long for viewers who discovered Fran and Teacher during the original broadcast.

The production later confirmed the 2026 window and gradually revealed the returning staff, Floating Island visual and trailers before finally locking in the September 30 advance-streaming date and October 7 television premiere.

A long gap can hurt a sequel if viewers forget why they cared. In this case, the marketing has wisely centered the two things most likely to bring fans back: Fran and Teacher's relationship, and a visibly larger adventure.
Should You Rewatch Season 1 Before Season 2?
A full rewatch is not absolutely necessary if you remember Fran's origin, Teacher's abilities and her goal of evolving, but it will make the sequel easier to follow.
Season 2 builds directly on Fran's growth as an adventurer. Her relationship with Teacher is already established, and the story is moving forward rather than introducing them again from scratch.
If you have been watching several reincarnation series between seasons, our
Tensura Season 4 guide
is also a useful reminder of how differently modern isekai handles progression: Rimuru builds political power on a massive scale, while Fran's ambition remains intensely personal.
What We Still Don't Know About Season 2
Even with the latest trailer, several details remain open.

The official site has not yet listed a final episode count. International streaming timing may differ from Japan's September 30 ABEMA premiere. The promotional campaign has also deliberately withheld some of the Floating Island's secrets.
Those are reasonable mysteries to leave for the broadcast.
What is confirmed is much more useful: the dates, central setting, major new characters, returning studio, main staff, cast and theme songs are all now public.
Why Reincarnated as a Sword Season 2 Is Worth Watching
There are plenty of isekai built around unusual reincarnations. Few make the gimmick feel as emotionally useful as
Reincarnated as a Sword

Teacher being a weapon means he cannot simply live the fantasy on his own. He needs a wielder. Fran being that wielder turns what could have been a joke premise into a story about two characters giving each other a future.

Season 2 seems ready to test that bond with a setting built for escalation. The Floating Island is full of undead monsters. Jean brings necromancy into the party. Nameless carries a mystery connected to the island. And the Lich is already being presented as the enemy Fran and Teacher must break through together.
The wait is almost over.
Reincarnated as a Sword Season 2 begins streaming on ABEMA on September 30, 2026, before its Japanese TV broadcast starts October 7.
For international fans, HIDIVE has announced the sequel for its 2026 lineup, with regional scheduling details worth checking closer to launch.
